Opilatio instrumentorum, vel compressio.
units.tr: They arise from urgent need, an obedient faculty, and a fault of the instruments; or from a remarkable abundance of humours. Fault of the instruments: strong obstruction, violent compression. Quick on both sides, before and after the rest: a faculty that raises and preserves its strength and struggles against the abundance of humours. The other differences are evident from these. They produce the caprizans pulse: an excessive abundance of humours; obstruction of the instruments, or compression.

units.la: Cum motus est perpetuus, quanquam disparis celeritatis.
units.tr: When the motion is continuous, though of unequal speed.

units.la: Pulsus itaque ab initio ad finem usque, in celeritatem assurgentes parit: Facultas minus onerata. Contra habentes: Magis onerata. Nullos tales parit: Facultas oppressa, cum omnes tales magni sint. Pulsum in contraria affatim mutatum: Facultas grauata. Instrumentorum obstructio, vel pressio.
units.tr: Thus a pulse that rises in speed from beginning to end arises from a faculty less burdened. The contrary, from one more burdened. It produces no such pulses: a faculty oppressed, since all such pulses are large. A pulse abruptly changed into the contrary: a faculty weighed down; obstruction or pressure of the instruments.

units.la: Cum
units.tr: When

units.la: Cũ motus est reciprocus, Dicrotos oftendũt:
units.tr: When the motion is reciprocal, they show a dicrotous pulse:

units.la: Vibratorum causæ.
units.tr: Causes of the vibrating pulse.

units.la: Vibratum pariunt: Valida facultas. Instrumentum durum. Vsus vrgens.
units.tr: The vibrating pulse arises from a strong faculty, a hard instrument, and pressing use.

units.la: Vsum urgent: Caloris abundantia. Spiritus animalis exhauslus.
units.tr: Pressing use is produced by an abundance of heat and exhausted animal spirit.

units.la: Dicrotum interdum pariunt: Magna intéperies, et parua arteriæ durities.
units.tr: Sometimes they produce the dicrotous pulse: a great intemperies and a slight hardness of the artery.

units.la: Interdum: Durities ingens, cum quadam intemperie, vel crassitudine, vel abundantia humorum, vel carnis.
units.tr: Sometimes: great hardness, with some intemperies, or thickness, or an abundance of humours or of flesh.

units.la: Myuros: Facultatis imbecillitas, vel per se vel ob pondus incumbentium corporum.
units.tr: Myurus: weakness of the faculty, either in itself or because of the weight of the bodies lying upon it.

units.la: Vndosos: Facultas modicè affecta. Humida mollisque arteria.
units.tr: Undulating: a moderately affected faculty; a moist and soft artery.

units.la: Vermiculantes: Facultas insigniter debilitata. Mollis arteria.
units.tr: Vermicular: a markedly weakened faculty; a soft artery.

units.la: Formicantem uermiculanti: Succedere iam est dictum. Conuulsiuum facit:Neruorum tensio, coniuncto vniuerso ner-norum genere cum arteryis, propter commu-nem affectum.
units.tr: The formicant pulse, which resembles the vermicular, has already been discussed. It produces a convulsive pulse: tension of the nerves, with the whole kind of nerves joined to the arteries on account of their common affection.

units.la: Tremulum:Facultas imbecilla.Arteria mollis. &,Corporis gracilis habitus.
units.tr: Tremulous: a feeble faculty; a soft artery; and a slender habit of body.

units.la: Serrantem, uel secantem, uel serratum:Arteriarum durities ex inflammatione, & earundem intemperies, in vno occursu inaequales.
units.tr: Serrating, sawing, or serrated: hardness of the arteries from inflammation, and their intemperies, uneven at a single encounter.

units.la: Pulsum hecticum:Febris, quae corporis occupauit uniuersum habitum.
units.tr: Hectic pulse: a fever that has taken hold of the whole habit of the body.

units.la: Quales fiant ab externis causis pulsuum mutationes,Ex libro de pulsibus, ad eos qui introducun-tur, tibi est perdiscendum.
units.tr: How changes of the pulse arise from external causes you must thoroughly learn from the book on pulses, in the part addressed to those being introduced to it.

units.la: DE PVLSVVM IVDICIIS, vel praenidentijs.
units.tr: ON THE JUDGMENTS OF PULSES, OR PROGNOSES.

units.la: Pulsus magnus, nō uno dicitur modo. Nempe,AVT ad moderatum comparatus:Aut ad naturalem cuiusque.Magnus
units.tr: A large pulse is not spoken of in only one way. Namely, it is judged either compared with the moderate pulse, or compared with each person's natural pulse.

units.la: Magnus ad naturalem cuiusque, duplex: Nempe, Aut minor moderato: Aut maior.
units.tr: A large pulse compared with each person's natural pulse is twofold: namely, either smaller than the moderate, or larger.

units.la: Consideratur uterq;, tum ad moderatum, tum ad naturalem cuiusque, Vel in sanis, qui ab omni motu sint liberi: Vel in ijs, quibus motus aduentitius est coniunctus: Vel in aegrotantibus tantum: Vel quibus recēs aliqua externa sit alteratio.
units.tr: Each of these is considered both in relation to the moderate and in relation to each person's natural pulse: either in the healthy, who are free from all motion; or in those to whom an additional motion is joined; or in the sick only; or in those in whom some recent external alteration has occurred.

units.la: Magnus ad moderatum in sanis, ab omni motu liberis: Temperamentum annunciat: Aut, Corporis habitudinem.
units.tr: A large pulse compared with the moderate in the healthy, free from all motion, indicates a temperament, or the condition of the body.

units.la: Magnus ad naturalem cuiusq; in eisdem: Calorem accessisse, aut gracilitatem.
units.tr: A large pulse compared with each one's natural pulse in the same people indicates that heat has been added, or slenderness.

units.la: Nam si maior fuerit, Calorem accessisse, seu vsum immutatum.
units.tr: For if it is larger, heat has been added, or else the usual condition is unchanged.

units.la: Si non maior factus, sed tantum uideatur, Corpus gracilius euasisse.
units.tr: If it has become no larger but only seems to be, the body has become more slender.

units.la: In quibus adiuctus est aduentitius motus: Motus, cui pulsus magnus est familiaris, vi Etoriam.
units.tr: In those in whom an additional motion is joined: the victory of that motion to which a large pulse is familiar.

units.la: In aegrotis: Morbi calidum affectum.
units.tr: In the sick: the hot affection of the disease.

units.la: D
units.tr: D

units.la: In quibus recens aliqua, quæ externa sit, alteratio:
units.tr: In those in whom some recent alteration, which is external, has occurred:

units.la: Victoriam motus illius, cui pulsus magnus est peculiaris.
units.tr: The victory of that motion to which a large pulse is peculiar.

units.la: Motus aduenticij, calfacientes sunt,
units.tr: Additional motions are heating:

units.la: Exercitatio.
units.tr: Exercise.

units.la: Cibus.
units.tr: Food.

units.la: Potus.
units.tr: Drink.

units.la: Balnea.
units.tr: Baths.

units.la: Medicamenta.
units.tr: Medicines.

units.la: Animi affectus, & similia.
units.tr: Affections of the mind, and the like.

units.la: Minorem solito citra facultatis imbecillitatem, & arteriæ duritiam parit:
units.tr: A pulse smaller than usual, without weakness of the faculty and hardness of the artery, produces:

units.la: Vsus remissus.
units.tr: Relaxed use.

units.la: Vsus remissionem,
units.tr: Use brings about remission,

units.la: Refrigeratio.
units.tr: Cooling.

units.la: Refrigerantes causæ: Aër frigidus, Balneum frigidum. Aqua frigida, Medicamentum inunctum. Longa quies: Veluti latebræ.
units.tr: Cooling causes: cold air, a cold bath, cold water, an ointment applied to the skin, long rest such as lying hidden.

units.la: Quæ intrò recipiuntur: vt aër, cibus pituito sus, frigida vsus immodicus.
units.tr: Things taken in internally: such as air, phlegmatic food, and excessive cold drink.

units.la: Ex animi affectibus, metus diuturnus.
units.tr: From affections of the mind: prolonged fear.

units.la: Contenti in corpore, frigidi humores.
units.tr: Cold humours contained in the body.

units.la: Pulsuum igitur in magnitudine, & paruita te mute mutationes, quod ad rei naturā pertinet, à tot et talibus fiunt causis: sed quòd ad nostrā cognitionem attinet, hoc non sufficit. Nempe saepius arteria quantum in se est, maximè distenditur: sed occultatur distensionis magnitudo, vel interpellatur à circunjacentiū corporum, vel obiectorū, aut numero, aut crassitie, aut duritie.
units.tr: Changes in the size and smallness of pulses, as far as the nature of the thing is concerned, come from so many and such causes; but as far as our knowledge is concerned, this is not enough. Indeed, the artery, as far as it is in itself, is often most distended, but the magnitude of the distension is hidden, or it is obstructed by the surrounding bodies or the obstacles in its way, whether by their number, their thickness or their hardness.

units.la: Quæ arterijs obijciuntur: Certæ membranæ. Cutis. Adeps multis locis, & caro.
units.tr: What is placed over the arteries: certain membranes, the skin. Fat in many places, and flesh.

units.la: Motus si occultetur omnis, atque in omnibus arteriæ partibus: Asphyxia vocatur.
units.tr: If all motion is hidden, in every part of the artery, it is called asphyxia.

units.la: Si in quibusdam partibus moueri arteria vi deatur, in alijs non: Differentiā in longitudine habent pulsus.
units.tr: If the artery seems to move in some parts but not in others, pulses differ in length.

units.la: Nempe de motu arteriarum, tantum animad uertitur, quantum permittunt opposita corpora.
units.tr: Indeed, only as much of the motion of the arteries is perceived as the opposing bodies allow.

units.la: Hinc corpulentorū pulsus, breues: graciliū, longi. Sed non æquè impediuntur latitudo & profunditas. Nempe ubi arteriarum regiones in obliquo, vel adipis, uel carnis, vel va porum, vel humorum plenæ sunt, ac incumbens superne cutis nihil eas oneret, latitudinis tantum obscuratur motus, & magis si pulsus vehemens & magnus sit. Cum vero regiones vicinæ mudæ sint: rugosa vero, quæ eas tegit, cutis, profunditatis motus magis latet: & magis, si non vehemens & magnus sit pulsus. Sed de latis & profundis pulsibus, dictum est in causis pulsuum.
units.tr: Hence the pulses of the corpulent are short, and those of the slender long. But breadth and depth are not equally impeded. Namely, where the regions of the arteries lie obliquely and are full of fat, or flesh, or veins, or humours, and the skin lying above does not weigh on them, only the motion in breadth is obscured, and more so if the pulse is vehement and large. But when the neighbouring regions are bare, yet the wrinkled skin covering them, the motion in depth is more hidden, and more so if the pulse is not vehement and large. But concerning broad and deep pulses, it has been said in the causes of pulses.

units.la: Vehemens pulsus, cum à facultatis robore semper fiat:
units.tr: A vehement pulse, since it always arises from the strength of the faculty:

units.la: Quo vehementior, tanto robur facultatis maius.
units.tr: The more vehement the pulse, the greater the strength of the faculty.

units.la: Robur facultatis augentia: Alia in corpore sunt: Alia extrinsecus adueniunt.
units.tr: Things that increase the strength of the faculty: some are in the body, others come from outside.

units.la: Quæ in corpore sunt: Humores semicoctli, quæ iam coquuntur. Naturæ ad indicationem impetus. Ira.
units.tr: Those in the body: semi-cooked humours which are now being cooked; nature's impulse towards the indication; anger.

units.la: Quæ extrinsecus adueniunt: Vinu, cibus, exercitationes modicæ, & quæ cordis arteriarumq; corrigunt intemperiem. Languidus, cū ex facultatis imbecillitate fit, Quo languidior, eo facultatem imbecilliorem annunciat.
units.tr: Those that come from outside: wine, food, moderate exercises, and whatever corrects the intemperature of the heart and arteries. A languid pulse, when it arises from weakness of the faculty, indicates that the faculty is weaker the more languid it is.

units.la: Si nunc languidus, nunc uehemens: Facultatem non per se imbecillam, sed humorum copia degrauatam.
units.tr: If now languid, now vehement: the faculty is not weak in itself, but weighed down by an abundance of humours.

units.la: Facultatem debilitari non est, nisi corpus cordis intemperatum esse, vel refrigeratum, vel calfactum, vel humectatum, vel desiccatum.
units.tr: The faculty is weakened only if the substance of the heart is intemperate, either cooled, or heated, or moistened, or dried.

units.la: Duri pulsus, uel mollis quantitas: Arteriæ quantitatem in duritie, vel mollitudine ostendit.
units.tr: Hard or soft pulses: the quantity of the artery is shown by its hardness or softness.

units.la: Arteriarum tunicas indurant: Inflammatio. Frigiditas. Potus frigidæ. Meracius vinum. Scirrhosus affectus. Aqua sulphurea, & aluminosa. Exsiccantia medicamenta. Atrophia, & similia.
units.tr: They harden the coats of the arteries: inflammation, cold, cold drinks, stronger wine, a scirrhous affection, sulphurous and aluminous water, drying medicines, atrophy, and the like.

units.la: Durissimus, ut mollissimus, periculosus: Nempe ex scirrho, aut inflammatione insigni viscceris, aut constrictione per frigus, aut ex siccitate ab ardentissima febre, aut ex ualida convulsione. Hic ex alto comate, aqua intercute, leucophlegmatia, & simpliciter ex immodica humiditate.
units.tr: The hardest, like the softest, is dangerous: namely, from a scirrhus, or a marked inflammation of an internal organ, or constriction from cold, or dryness from a very burning fever, or from a violent convulsion. The hardest comes from deep coma, dropsy, leucophlegmasia, and simply from excessive moisture.

units.la: Celer pulsus, bifariam dicitur:
units.tr: A quick pulse is spoken of in two ways:

units.la: Ad moderatum comparatus:
units.tr: Compared with the moderate:

units.la: Ad quemlibet alium sanum.
units.tr: Compared with any other healthy person.

units.la: Bifariam uterq; consideratur:
units.tr: Each is considered in two ways:

units.la: In sanis:
units.tr: In the healthy:

units.la: In affectis corporibus.
units.tr: In diseased bodies.

units.la: Celerior in sanis:
units.tr: Quicker in the healthy:

units.la: Calidius temperamentum.
units.tr: A hotter temperament.

units.la: In affectis corporibus:
units.tr: In diseased bodies:

units.la: Vsus incrementum.
units.tr: An increase of use.

units.la: Tardior in sanis:
units.tr: Slower in the healthy:

units.la: Frigidius temperamentum.
units.tr: A colder temperament.

units.la: In affectis corporibus:
units.tr: In diseased bodies:

units.la: Vsus remissionem.
units.tr: Remission of use.

units.la: Creber item bifariam:
units.tr: Likewise frequent, in two ways:

units.la: Quiete externa:
units.tr: From external rest:

units.la: Quiete interna.
units.tr: From internal rest.

units.la: Quiete externa:
units.tr: From external rest:

units.la: Vel productam distensionem:
units.tr: Either a prolonged distension:

units.la: Vel anticipantem contractionem.
units.tr: Or an anticipated contraction.

units.la: Producta distensio:
units.tr: Prolonged distension:

units.la: Calorem purum increuisse. Anticipans contractio: Impuri, atque excrementosi copiam. Creber quiete interna: Aut productionem contractionis: Aut anticipationem distensionis. Productio contractionis: Fumosorum excrementorum copiam. Anticipatio distensionis: Auctum calorem. Rarus externa quiete: Vel imminutam distensionem: Vel moram contractionis. Distensio imminuta: Refrigeratum calorem. Mora contractionis: Imminuta, fumosa excrementa. Rarus quiete interna: Vel imminutam contractionem, Vel distensionis moram. Contractio imminuta: Pauciora excrementa. Distensionis mora: Imminutum calorem.
units.tr: Pure heat has increased. Anticipated contraction: a quantity of impure and excrementitious matter. Frequent from internal rest: either a prolonged contraction, or an anticipated distension. Prolonged contraction: a quantity of smoky excrements. Anticipated distension: increased heat. Rare from external rest: either a diminished distension, or a delay in contraction. Diminished distension: cooled heat. Delay in contraction: diminished, smoky excrements. Rare from internal rest: either a diminished contraction, or a delay in distension. Diminished contraction: fewer excrements. Delay in distension: diminished heat.

units.la: Si coniuncta ambo, ut motus prior proten datur, alter anticipet in quiete utraque: Compositum affectum.
units.tr: If both are joined, so that the first motion is prolonged and the other anticipates, in either rest: a compound affection.

units.la: Pulsus hi omnes, non tantum per se consi-derantur, sed & inter se iuncti, ut magnus, & vehemens, qualis est iratorum: magnus, celeris, & creber, ut in ardentissimis febri-bus. At horum cognitio ex his quae per se per-penduntur, est petenda.
units.tr: All these pulses are considered not only on their own, but also joined together: as large and vehement, such as that of angry people; large, quick and frequent, as in the most burning fevers. But knowledge of these must be sought from those things which are weighed on their own.

units.la: Pulsus intermittens in collectiua inæqua-litate: Facultatem degrauatam, Vel distensionis prohibitionem.
units.tr: An intermittent pulse, in collective inequality: a weighed-down faculty, or a prevention of distension.

units.la: Facultatem degrauant: Humorum copia, vel crassitudo, uel spaciorum, in quibus arteriæ distenduntur, occupatio.
units.tr: They weigh down the faculty: an abundance or thickness of humours, or the occupation of the spaces in which the arteries are distended.

units.la: Distensionem prohibent: Inflammatio. Scirrhus, vel tumor alius.
units.tr: They prevent distension: inflammation, scirrhus, or some other tumour.

units.la: Pulsus intermittentis quies gemina: Diuturna. Breuis.
units.tr: The rest of an intermittent pulse is twofold: prolonged and brief.

units.la: Diuturna: Quae excedit duorum pulsuum tempus.
units.tr: Prolonged: that which exceeds the time of two pulses.

units.la: Breuis: Quae intra manet.
units.tr: Brief: that which remains within that limit.

units.la: Diuturna: Difficulter tollitur.
units.tr: Prolonged: is removed with difficulty.

units.la: Breuis: Non citra negotium: vt de apoplexia dicitur. Hæc item moderatissima, ex qua senes multi & pueri euaserunt: iuuenum nullus.
units.tr: Brief: not without trouble, as is said of apoplexy. This is also very moderate, and from it many old men and boys have escaped; of young men, none.

units.la: Intermittens igitur omnium inæqualium perniciosissimus: Quòd in motus sit abolitione.
units.tr: Intermittence, then, is the most deadly of all irregular pulses: because motion is abolished.

units.la: Iuuenibus perniciosus magis: Quòd firma facultates à maximis occasioni bus tantum deiciantur.
units.tr: More deadly to the young: because firm faculties are overthrown only by the greatest occasions.

units.la: Pueris minus: Quia à minoribus offendantur causis, facultate scilicet imbecilliore. Quia ité concoctrice firmiore, quæ facilè offensas corrigat: corpore item mollissimo, & perspirabili.
units.tr: Less so for boys: because they are offended by smaller causes, namely a weaker faculty; also because the concocting faculty is firmer and easily corrects offences; also because the body is very soft and perspirable.

units.la: Senibus minimè: Quòd imbecillæ facultates, à paruis sæpe occasionibus offendantur.
units.tr: Least of all in old men: because weak faculties are often offended by small occasions.

units.la: Intermittens pulsus à raritate longa distat: Quòd scilicet raritas longa, temporis sit longioris: item quòd interdum pulsuum omnium æqualitatem habet.
units.tr: An intermittent pulse differs from long rarity: because long rarity belongs to a longer time, and also because sometimes it has the equality of all pulses.

units.la: Intermittens, necessariò inæqualis.
units.tr: Intermittent, necessarily unequal.

units.la: Raritatem longam parit: Ingens frigiditas, quæ corpus occupet cordis, vel spiritum & sanguinem, vel partem aliquam vicinam.
units.tr: It produces long rarity: a great coldness, which occupies the body of the heart, or the spirit and blood, or some neighbouring part.

units.la: Raritas illa perniciosa:
units.tr: That rarity is deadly:

units.la: Quòd nonnulli inter dormiendum, moriuntur, & nunquam expergiscuntur.
units.tr: Some die while asleep, and never wake.

units.la: Alij tum hoc modo, tum inter loquendum alijs prorumpit sudor, alijs non.
units.tr: In some, sweat breaks out then, or while speaking; in others not.

units.la: Hic affectus, aegrotantes quosdam corripit: cum insperato, & praeter omnem rationem febre liberentur: Alios item sanos, & potissimum in senectute.
units.tr: This affection seizes some sick people, who are freed from fever unexpectedly and beyond all reason; it also seizes healthy people, and especially in old age.

units.la: Ab intermittentibus pulsibus:
units.tr: From intermittent pulses:

units.la: Mors repentina corripit, non aliter, quàm ab apoplexia.
units.tr: Sudden death seizes, no differently than from apoplexy.

units.la: Intercurrens, qui ex crebritate inaequali fit, quòd minus plena fuerit cordis functio, quàm postularet usus:
units.tr: An intercurrent pulse, which arises from irregular frequency, because the function of the heart is less full than use demands:

units.la: Cor humoru copia oneratum ostendit, aut in strumenta obstructa, aut in arctu coacta.
units.tr: The heart shows itself burdened by an abundance of humours, either obstructed in its organs or constrained in its narrowness.

units.la: Intercurrens pulsus, saepe
units.tr: An intercurrent pulse often

units.la: Iudicationem attulit, natura vehementer ad depugnandum parata.
units.tr: has brought about a crisis, nature being strongly prepared to fight it out.

units.la: Intermittens in pulsu uno, ubi distensionem interpellat quies, multas habet species: & omnes quidem periculosas, omnisque talis nunciat: Certare naturam cum insalubribus causis, et ab illis simul impediri.
units.tr: An intermittence in one pulse, where rest interrupts the distension, has many species: and all of them are indeed dangerous, and all such signify that nature contends with unhealthy causes and is at the same time impeded by them.

units.la: Si posterior motus, priore sit uehementior, Commodior.
units.tr: If the later beat is stronger than the earlier one, more favourable.

units.la: Si languidior, Periculosior.
units.tr: If weaker, more dangerous.

units.la: Si item tardior, Periculosior.
units.tr: If likewise slower, more dangerous.

units.la: Si celerior, Melior.
units.tr: If faster, better.

units.la: Intermittens ille pessimus: Cuius tempus quietis, sit prolixius.
units.tr: The intermittent pulse is the worst of all: its pause of rest is longer.

units.la: Intermittens in pulsu uno: Praesentem morem saepius denunciat.
units.tr: An intermittent pulse with a single missed beat often signals the present course of the disease.

units.la: Caprizans est huiusmodi, qui Inaequalem cordis intemperiem, nonnunquam comitatur.
units.tr: The caprizans is of this kind, which often accompanies an unequal disorder of the heart.

units.la: Dicrotus indicat, Inaequalem cordis intemperiem, quae corpus ipsum teneat.
units.tr: The dicrotus indicates an unequal disorder of the heart, one that holds the body itself.

units.la: Affectum illum, qui perdidit externam quietem.
units.tr: That affection which has lost its external rest.

units.la: Illum item, cuius impeditur distensio.
units.tr: Likewise that in which the dilatation is impeded.

units.la: Inaequalem quidem cordis intemperiem, ubi scilicet,
units.tr: An unequal disorder of the heart, namely where

units.la: Collectus sit in multis eius partibus fuliginosorum excrementorum aceruus. Nam si par tes quædam sint præcalidæ, aliæ fumosa suli gine præfocentur, ad cōtrarios prosilient mo tus, vt aliæ distensionem moliantur, aliæ con tractionem: sitque pugna hæc tribus modis:
units.tr: a heap of sooty excrements has collected in many of its parts. For if some parts are very hot, while others are choked with smoky soot, they leap into opposite motions, so that some attempt dilatation and others contraction. This struggle takes place in three ways:

units.la: Primò,
units.tr: First,

units.la: Cùm distensionem incompletam excipiat cō tractio.
units.tr: when contraction follows an incomplete dilatation.

units.la: Secundò,
units.tr: Second,

units.la: Cū prorsus completæ succedat, externa quie te perdita.
units.tr: when it follows a dilatation that is fully complete, the external rest having been lost.

units.la: Tertiò,
units.tr: Third,

units.la: Cùm nondum absolutam motus contrarius retrahat, qui debilior redditus, reliquum si nat compleri.
units.tr: when the opposing motion draws back before the dilatation is finished; the motion, being made weaker, allows the remainder to be completed.

units.la: Vermiculans:
units.tr: The vermiculans (wormlike pulse):

units.la: Infirmam facultatem.
units.tr: a weak faculty.

units.la: Vndosus, interdum
units.tr: The undulating pulse, sometimes:

units.la: Non firmam esse, non continuò tamen infir mam.
units.tr: not firm, yet not constantly weak.

units.la: Interdum:
units.tr: Sometimes:

units.la: Mediocriter firmam: & præsertim cùm su dorem decretorium promittit.
units.tr: moderately firm, and especially when it promises a decisive sweat.

units.la: Vndosus sequitur:
units.tr: The undulating pulse follows:

units.la: Morbos humidos, pituitosos’ citra scirrhū & & inflammationem.
units.tr: in moist, phlegmatic diseases, short of scirrhus and inflammation.

units.la: Lethargum.
units.tr: Lethargy.

units.la: Febres quotidianas, & quæ ἑλώδεις & τυ-
units.tr: Quotidian fevers, and those called helodes [ἑλώδεις] and

units.la: φώδεις vocantur.
units.tr: typhodes [τυφώδεις].

units.la: Anasarca.
units.tr: Anasarca.

units.la: Et morbos hos, quibus immodica humidita-
units.tr: And those diseases by which the lung rots from immoderate

units.la: te putruit pulmo.
units.tr: moisture.

units.la: Vermiculans:
units.tr: The vermiculans (wormlike pulse):

units.la: Largas vacuationes, sanguinis profluuia, al-
units.tr: Large evacuations, flows of blood, other discharges, cholera,

units.la: ui fluores, choleras, purgationes validas, vo-
units.tr: strong purgings, violent vomiting,

units.la: mitus fortes, vrinas copiosas, menses immo-
units.tr: copious urine, immoderate menses,

units.la: dicos, fluorem mulicbrem, sudores prauos.
units.tr: women's discharges, foul sweats.

units.la: Myurus duplex:
units.tr: The double myurus (mouse-tail pulse):

units.la: Alter in vna arteriæ distensione:
units.tr: One in a single dilatation of the artery;

units.la: Alter in aceruo.
units.tr: the other in a heap.

units.la: In una distensione:
units.tr: In a single dilatation:

units.la: Facultatis imbecillitatem:
units.tr: weakness of the faculty,

units.la: Vnà & corporis gracilitatem.
units.tr: together with slenderness of body.

units.la: Facultatis quidem imbecillitatem:
units.tr: Weakness of the faculty, indeed:

units.la: Quòd in myuris paulatim robur remittatur,
units.tr: because in the myurus the strength gradually relaxes,

units.la: tantoq; solito imbecillior efficiatur, quàm est
units.tr: and it becomes weaker than usual, in proportion as it is removed

units.la: à principio remota.
units.tr: from its beginning.

units.la: Myurus in aceruo:
units.tr: Myurus in a heap:

units.la: Facultatis imbecillitate, etiã sine gracilitate.
units.tr: weakness of the faculty, even without slenderness.

units.la: Myurus reciprocus: Minus cæteris exitialis. Tremulus:
units.tr: Reciprocal myurus: less deadly than the others. The tremulous pulse:

units.la: Facultatem imbecillam.
units.tr: a weak faculty,

units.la: Tunicam arteriæ mollem.
units.tr: a soft arterial coat,

units.la: Et corporis gracilem habitum. Vibratio:
units.tr: and a slender habit of body. The vibrating pulse:

units.la: Duræ arteriæ symptoma, est cum amplius cogitur vidistendi, sed tum durior revera non fit: sed violenter impulsa, ut distendatur amplius, hoc habet symptoma.
units.tr: It is a symptom of a hard artery: it occurs when the artery is forced to dilate more, yet it does not in truth become harder; rather, being violently struck so as to dilate further, it shows this symptom.

units.la: DE PVLSIBVS PASSIONI cuique peculiaribus.
units.tr: ON THE PULSES PECULIAR TO EACH AFFECTION.

units.la: Passio, quicquid præter naturā est, existit. Peculiare, quod passionem comitatur, vel perpetuò, vel magna ex parte. Quod præter naturam est:
units.tr: Passion is whatever exists contrary to nature. A peculiar sign accompanies the passion, either always or for the most part. What is contrary to nature:

units.la: Affectus:
units.tr: Affection:

units.la: Causa:
units.tr: Cause:

units.la: Symptoma. Affectus:
units.tr: Symptom. Affections:

units.la: Similares.
units.tr: Similar.

units.la: Instrumentarij. Similares:
units.tr: Instrumental. Similar:

units.la: Intemperies, tum simplices, tum compositæ. Calidæ cordis intemperiei, non uarianti-bus à corde arterijs:
units.tr: Intemperaments, both simple and compound. Hot intemperament of the heart, with arteries not differing from the heart:

units.la: Magnus, celer, creber, quanquā nō perpetuò.Si ad magnitudinem plus declinet:Calorem cordis, non ita copiosum.
units.tr: Large, quick, frequent, though not perpetually. If it leans more to largeness: heat of the heart, not so abundant.

units.la: Si ad celeritatem,Maiorem.
units.tr: If to quickness: greater heat.

units.la: Si ad crebritatem,Adhuc maiorem.
units.tr: If to frequency: greater still.

units.la: Maximus, celerrimus, creberrimus:Summum caloris incrementum.
units.tr: Largest, quickest, most frequent: the highest increase of heat.

units.la: Celerrimus, creberrimus, non maximus:Calorem quidem copiosum, sed facultate im-becillam, vel arteriam duriorem.
units.tr: Quickest, most frequent, not largest: heat indeed abundant, but the faculty weak, or the artery harder.

units.la: Creberrimus, non celerrimus, nec maxi-mus:Copiosum item calorem: sed vel facultatis im-becillitatem, vel instrumentorū duritiem.
units.tr: Most frequent, not quickest nor largest: likewise abundant heat, but either weakness of the faculty or hardness of the instruments.

units.la: Imbecillitatem comitatur:Languidus.
units.tr: Accompanied by weakness: languid.

units.la: Duritiem:Durus pariter, & vibratus.
units.tr: Accompanied by hardness: hard and also vibrating.

units.la: Si durus, non uibratus, & summè creber, & iam unà languidus:Calorem multū indicat, & facultatem im-becillam, & ob id syncopam minatur.
units.tr: If hard, not vibrating, most frequent, and already languid as well: indicates much heat and a weak faculty, and therefore threatens syncope.

units.la: Calor cordis geminus:
units.tr: The twofold heat of the heart:

units.la: Qui sola quantitate variat, Fumosus.
units.tr: which varies by quantity alone: smoky.

units.la: Fumosus:
units.tr: Smoky:

units.la: Breuem habet quietem internam, & celeriorem contractionem.
units.tr: has a short internal rest and a quicker contraction.

units.la: Sola quantitate uarians:
units.tr: Varying by quantity alone:

units.la: Maiorem, & celeriorem distensionem.
units.tr: a greater and quicker dilatation.

units.la: Fumosus:
units.tr: Smoky:

units.la: Constans, & obstirmatus.
units.tr: constant and obstinate.

units.la: Sola quantitate uarians:
units.tr: Varying by quantity alone:

units.la: Non diuturnus: qui balneas comitatur, exercitationes, cibos calidos, vini potu, animi affectus, verecundiam, & iram.
units.tr: not lasting long; it accompanies baths, exercise, warm foods, drinking wine, emotions of the mind, shame, and anger.

units.la: Cor si calidius, & arteriæ frigidiores, uel pro prio affectu, uel quòd frigidos continent humores:
units.tr: If the heart is hotter and the arteries cooler, either from their own affection or because they contain cold humours:

units.la: Medij pulsus erunt, moderati & naturales.
units.tr: the pulses will be middling, moderate and natural.

units.la: Cor si calidius, & materiæ frigidiores, tri- bus fit modis:
units.tr: If the heart is hotter and the humours colder, this happens in three ways:

units.la: Aut tantò calidius, quantò hæ frigidiores. Aut multò calidius, quàm hæ frigidiores: Aut minus calidius, quàm hæ frigidiores.
units.tr: either the heart is as much hotter as these are colder; or much hotter than these are colder; or less hot than these are cold.

units.la: Si primum,
units.tr: If the first,

units.la: Pulsus moderatus, magnitudine, celeritate, & crebritate.
units.tr: a pulse moderate in size, speed and frequency.

units.la: Si secundum, Maiores, celeriores, & crebriores, & natu-ralibus languidiores.
units.tr: If the second, greater, quicker and more frequent, and somewhat weaker than natural.

units.la: Si tertium, Minores, & rariores, celeritate naturalibus similes, vel tardiores.
units.tr: If the third, smaller and rarer, similar in speed to natural, or slower.

units.la: Cordis corpus, si iusto frigidius, & cordis attingentia calidiora, trifariam fit:
units.tr: If the body of the heart is colder than is right and the parts touching the heart are hotter, this happens in three ways:

units.la: Aut æque refrigeratum cor, ut incaluerunt attingentia:
units.tr: either the heart is cooled as much as the touching parts have warmed;

units.la: Aut multò frigidius, quàm hæc calidiora: Aut minus frigidius, quàm hæc calidiora.
units.tr: or it is much colder than these hotter parts; or less cold than these hotter parts.

units.la: Si primum, Pulsus tardior æquo, si insignis fuerit altera-tio: sed magnitudine, & crebritate modera-tus.
units.tr: If the first, a pulse slower than is right, if the alteration is marked; but moderate in size and frequency.

units.la: Si secundum, Languidior, minor, & non aperte tardus.
units.tr: If the second, weaker, smaller, and not openly slow.

units.la: Si tertium, Imbecillior, maior, & celerior naturali: sed maior, quàm celerior, & crebrior.
units.tr: If the third, weaker, larger, and quicker than natural: larger rather than quicker, and more frequent.

units.la: Pulsus hi moderatis similes, in eiusmodi pu-gnantia temperamentorum cordis optimos etiam fallunt medicos: nempe in pestilentijs tales contingunt. Quòd si inspiratus aër putridus, in cordis deflexerit corpus, tales sunt pulsus, & omnes pereunt.
units.tr: These pulses resemble moderate ones, and in such conflicting states of the heart's temperament they even deceive the best physicians. Indeed such pulses occur in pestilences. But if putrid air, breathed in, has settled upon the body of the heart, such pulses appear, and all die.

units.la: Si aut in corpus cordis deflexerit, signa:
units.tr: If it has settled upon the body of the heart, the signs are:

units.la: Si febrem primum percipiant: deinde si non æqualiter perpetuo febricitent: & pulsum nō habeant prævalidum. Nempe pulsus omnes imbecilli, qui corporis cordis intemperiem comitantur.
units.tr: if they first feel a fever; then if the fever is not even and continuous; and if they do not have a very strong pulse. Indeed all the pulses are weak which accompany an intemperament of the body of the heart.

units.la: Si talis aër inspiratus, ad humores deflexerit,
units.tr: If such air, breathed in, has settled upon the humours,

units.la: Multi euadunt.
units.tr: many escape.

units.la: Omnia hæc accipienda sunt, pulsibus, nec in mollitudinem, nec in duritiam aperte mutatis.
units.tr: All these things are to be taken from the pulses, provided they are not clearly changed either into softness or into hardness.

units.la: Cordis frigidæ intemperiei peculiares pulsus:
units.tr: The peculiar pulses of the cold intemperament of the heart:

units.la: Parui, tardi, & rari.
units.tr: small, slow and rare.

units.la: Facultas si plurimum laboret, cum adiuncta frigiditate:
units.tr: If the faculty labours greatly, with added coldness:

units.la: Extreme parui, non tardi extremeimo moderatis, aliquando similes, & crebriores.
units.tr: extremely small, not slow; in extreme cases, sometimes similar to moderate pulses, and more frequent.

units.la: Si facultas paululum laboret, frigiditate plurimum uigente:
units.tr: If the faculty labours a little, with coldness prevailing greatly:

units.la: Rarissimi, modice parui, medio modo ad tarditatem.
units.tr: very rare, moderately small, in a middle way tending towards slowness.

units.la: Cor si frigidius, & arteriæ ex æquo calidiores, Moderatis similes.
units.tr: If the heart is colder and the arteries equally hotter: similar to moderate pulses.

units.la: Affectus hi, febre vacant, refrigerato dun taxat à succis frigidis, ijsque lentis & crassis corde. Inciduntque potissimum, vbi in pulmone eiusmodi continentur humores.
units.tr: These affections lack fever, the heart being cooled only by cold and thick juices. They occur chiefly when such humours are contained in the lung.

units.la: Corde & arteriis frigidioribus:Minores, tardiores, & rariores.
units.tr: With the heart and arteries colder: smaller, slower and rarer.

units.la: Corde frigidiore, & rodentium pleno excrementorum:Minor, et rarior diftesio: cotractio, celerior.
units.tr: With the heart colder, and the parts full of excrements: a smaller and rarer dilatation; the contraction quicker.

units.la: Ex his collige inæqualem cordis intemperiem, geminam esse:
units.tr: From these points, gather that the unequal intemperament of the heart is twofold:

units.la: Alteram in succis proprijs:Alteram in partibus solidis.
units.tr: one in its own juices, the other in the solid parts.

units.la: Ex succis proprijs profecta:Vna cum totius corporis fit palpitatione.
units.tr: Arising from its own juices: it occurs together with palpitation of the whole body.

units.la: Ex solidis,Absque palpitatione.
units.tr: From the solids: without palpitation.

units.la: Cor siccius si fuerit, hoc est bifariam:Vel arteriis ita affectis:Vel contrà.
units.tr: If the heart is drier, this is twofold: either with the arteries so affected, or the reverse.

units.la: Si primum,Pulsus durus.
units.tr: If the first, a hard pulse.

units.la: Si secundum,Medius.
units.tr: If the second, a middling pulse.

units.la: Cor siccius reddunt:Victus siccus, medicamentorum exiccantium esus & potio, vinum merum, cibi defectus, potus, labor immodicus, senium, solicitudo, tristicia, diutinae vigiliae, marasmus.
units.tr: They make the heart drier: dry diet, use and drinking of drying medicines, undiluted wine, lack of food, drink, excessive labour, old age, anxiety, sadness, long wakefulness, marasmus.

units.la: Arterias desiccant:
units.tr: They dry the arteries:

units.la: Aqua sulphurea, aluminosa: & quaecunque exsiccant, ut medicamenta:
units.tr: sulphurous and aluminous water, and whatever dries, such as medicines;

units.la: Atrophia.
units.tr: atrophy.

units.la: Cordi humidiori, pulsus peculiaris,
units.tr: For a moister heart, the peculiar pulse is:

units.la: Mollis.
units.tr: soft.

units.la: Cor humidum reddunt:
units.tr: They make the heart moist:

units.la: Oedemata.
units.tr: oedemas,

units.la: Leucophlegmatias.
units.tr: leucophlegmasies.

units.la: Pulsum mollem, mediocris mollitudinis pariunt:
units.tr: They produce a soft pulse of moderate softness:

units.la: Cibi humidiores: ocium multum.
units.tr: moister foods, much idleness,

units.la: Somnus longus: balneae a cibo.
units.tr: long sleep, baths after food.

units.la: PVLSVS quonam modo per febres dignoscantur.
units.tr: How pulses are distinguished in fevers.

units.la: Diariarum omnium, quantum in ipsis est,
units.tr: Of all the daily fevers, as far as they themselves are concerned:

units.la: Magni, celeres, crebri.
units.tr: large, quick, frequent.

units.la: Quantum in ipsis dictum:
units.tr: As far as they are stated in themselves:

units.la: Quoniam alio concurrente affectu, mixta erit mutatio.
units.tr: since another affection concurring will make the change a mixed one.

units.la: Hecticarum quantum in ipsis est,
units.tr: Of the hectic fevers, as far as they themselves are concerned:

units.la: Idem, sed amplius celeres.
units.tr: the same, but quicker still.

units.la: Putridarum omnium cum inuadunt,
units.tr: When all putrid fevers attack,

units.la: Contractio celerior, & pulsus in quiete externa crebrior: natura scilicet ad id quod fumosum est, expellendum incumbente.
units.tr: the contraction is quicker, and the pulse in external rest more frequent, since nature is bent on expelling what is smoky.

units.la: Cum increscunt,
units.tr: When they increase,

units.la: Contractionis celeritas augetur: & pulsus in externa quiete crebritas.
units.tr: the speed of contraction increases, and the frequency of the pulse in external rest.

units.la: Cum uigent,
units.tr: When they are at their height,

units.la: Tum distensionis, tum contractionis æqua celeritas.
units.tr: the speed of dilatation and of contraction is equal.

units.la: Pulsus æqua quietum, tum internæ, tum externæ crebritas.
units.tr: The pulse is equally frequent in rest, both internal and external.

units.la: Cum declinant,
units.tr: When they decline,

units.la: Contractionis celeritas dissoluitur.
units.tr: the speed of contraction is dissolved.

units.la: Soli hi pulsus febrium, per se proprij sunt: reliqui omnes, qui febrientibus accidunt, affectum alium potius, quàm febres sequuntur: vt facultatis, vel instrumentorum: & propterea addenda hæc distinctio, si mutatio citra aliam acciderit occasionem.
units.tr: Only these pulses of fevers are proper to them alone. All the others which occur in feverish people follow some other affection rather than the fever, such as of the faculty or the instruments; and therefore this distinction must be added: whether the change occurs without any other occasion.

units.la: Occasio eiusmodi, duplex: Externa. Interna.
units.tr: There are two kinds of such a cause: external and internal.

units.la: Externa:
units.tr: External:

units.la: Cibus, potus, motus quiuis, & animi affectus.
units.tr: Food, drink, any motion, and states of mind.

units.la: Interna:
units.tr: Internal:

units.la: Vomitus, & vellicatio vitiosis succis in ven-trem confluentibus.Item cùm rigor, horror, inæqualitas & frigus fiunt.
units.tr: Vomiting, and a gnawing of the stomach from vicious juices flowing into the belly. Likewise when shivering, horror, irregularity and cold occur.

units.la: Confluente interdū, accessionis initio, ad cor materiæ frigidę & humidę aceruo, mor-tis periculum est, ne scilicet principium ex-tinguatur, cuius rei signum est:
units.tr: Sometimes at the onset of the paroxysm a mass of cold and moist matter gathers at the heart, and there is danger of death, namely that the principle may be extinguished. The sign of this is:

units.la: Pulsuum in raritatem, tarditatem, & par-uitatem mutatio.
units.tr: A change of the pulses to rarity, slowness and smallness.

units.la: Pulmonum affectui, qui pulsus peculiares, pulmonib. enim pröptissimè cor cösentit.
units.tr: This belongs to an affection of the lungs, which has its own pulses, since the heart most closely sympathises with the lungs.

units.la: Pulmonis affectus:
units.tr: Affections of the lungs:

units.la: Intemperies morbosa.
units.tr: Morbid intemperature.

units.la: Morbi plethorici ut erysipelas, vel inflam-matio, fluxio.
units.tr: Plethoric diseases such as erysipelas, or inflammation and fluxion.

units.la: Pulmone calfacto, si cor prauum calorem contraxerit:
units.tr: When the lungs are heated, if the heart has contracted a harmful heat:

units.la: Pulsus, vsus pulsuum auƈti comites.
units.tr: Pulses of the quickened kind, as companions.

units.la: Pulmonis calfacti signa:
units.tr: Signs of a heated lung:

units.la: Thoracis æstus.
units.tr: Heat of the chest.

units.la: Respiratio calida.
units.tr: Hot breathing.

units.la: Sitis, fauces calidiores, lingua calidior et sic-cor, et malo ingrauescēte aspera et atro colore
units.tr: Thirst, a hotter throat, a hotter and dry tongue, and, as the malady grows worse, a rough tongue of dark colour.

units.la: Pulmone refrigerato:
units.tr: When the lung is cooled:

units.la: Pulsus vsui dissoluto peculiares.
units.tr: Pulses peculiar to a loosened motion.

units.la: Pulmone sicciore, & corde consentiente:
units.tr: When the lung is drier and the heart agrees:

units.la: Pulsus duriores.
units.tr: Harder pulses.

units.la: Pulmonis siccioris, signa:
units.tr: Signs of a drier lung:

units.la: Faucium prompta, tametsi nihil sitiant, are scentia.
units.tr: A throat ready and dry, though not thirsty at all.

units.la: Pulmone humidiore:
units.tr: When the lung is moister:

units.la: Molles.
units.tr: Soft.

units.la: Pulmonis humidioris, signa:
units.tr: Signs of a moister lung:

units.la: Fauces humidiores, sitis nulla. Ex simplicib. intemperiebus, cognoscuntur composita.
units.tr: A moister throat, no thirst. Compound intemperatures are recognised from simple ones.

units.la: Pulmo, si fluxione afficiatur:
units.tr: If the lung is affected by a fluxion:

units.la: Pulsuum omnium est inæqualitas, eaq; nunc maior, nunc minor, pro humoris crassitudine, & abundantia.
units.tr: All the pulses are irregular, and this sometimes greater, sometimes less, according to the thickness and abundance of the humour.

units.la: Minor:
units.tr: Less:

units.la: Ex subtilibus & paucis.
units.tr: From thin and scanty humours.

units.la: Maior:
units.tr: Greater:

units.la: Ex crassis, lentis, & copiosis: quod principes arterias obstruant magis, comprimant & gravent.
units.tr: From thick, viscous and copious humours, because they obstruct the main arteries more, and compress and weigh them down.

units.la: Fluxio calidior, in cæteris differentijs pulsus habet,
units.tr: A hotter fluxion has the other differences of pulse,

units.la: Quales à copioso calore fiunt.
units.tr: such as arise from copious heat.

units.la: Si frigidior,
units.tr: If it is colder,

units.la: Quales à caloris defectu.
units.tr: such as arise from a lack of heat.

units.la: Si igitur fluxio eadem non est, neque suffocatio eadem:
units.tr: If therefore the fluxion is not the same, neither is the suffocation the same:

units.la: Nempe calidiorem potius suffocato comitatur, quòd largiorem spiritū natura trahi ex- postulat. Sola intemperies, nullum suffocatio nis excipit periculum.
units.tr: Namely, a hotter pulse rather accompanies suffocation, because nature requires that a larger breath be drawn. Intemperature alone admits no danger of suffocation.

units.la: Fluxio item cadit:
units.tr: A fluxion also falls:

units.la: Vel in solas asperas arterias:
units.tr: Either only on the rough arteries

units.la: Vel nunc in læues & venas.
units.tr: or now on the smooth arteries and veins.

units.la: Si in solas asperas:
units.tr: If only on the rough arteries:

units.la: Pulsus nihilo durior.
units.tr: The pulse is not at all harder.

units.la: Si in læues,
units.tr: If on the smooth:

units.la: Pulsus durior; quòd totius animalis arteriæ intendantur.
units.tr: The pulse is harder, because the arteries of the whole body are tensed.

units.la: Pulmone inflammato, & induratis tumoribus affecto:
units.tr: When the lung is inflamed and affected by hardened tumours:

units.la: Duriores:
units.tr: Harder.

units.la: Si œdematoso affectu uexetur:
units.tr: If it is troubled by an oedematous affection:

units.la: Molliores.
units.tr: Softer.

units.la: THORACI affecto, qui pulsus peculiares.
units.tr: The pulses peculiar to an affected CHEST:

units.la: Thoracis affectus:
units.tr: Affections of the chest:

units.la: Intemperaturæ.
units.tr: Intemperatures.

units.la: Tumores.
units.tr: Tumours.

units.la: Intemperaturæ:
units.tr: Intemperatures:

units.la: Pulsus habent tales, quales pulmonum intem peraturæ.
units.tr: The pulses have the same qualities as those of intemperatures of the lungs.

units.la: Tumores:
units.tr: Tumours:

units.la: Pro genere humorum eos procreantium.
units.tr: According to the kind of humours producing them.

units.la: Variant tamen utriq;:
units.tr: Yet they differ in both respects:

units.la: Quòd cor pulmoni, quàm thoraci magis con sentit.
units.tr: because the heart sympathises with the lung more than with the chest.

units.la: Quòd interdum affecta thoracis pars, interdum succingens costas tunica.
units.tr: because sometimes the affected part is the chest itself, and sometimes the membrane encircling the ribs.

units.la: Nempe si duræ partes & spissæ intumescant, maior tensio est.
units.tr: Namely, if hard and dense parts swell, there is greater tension.

units.la: Hinc pleuriticorum, quam peripneumonicorum pulsus,
units.tr: Hence the pulses of pleurisy sufferers, compared with those of peripneumonia,

units.la: Duriores.
units.tr: are harder.

units.la: In succingentium costas tunicarum tumribus,
units.tr: In tumours of the membranes encircling the ribs,

units.la: Pulsus æquales.
units.tr: the pulses are equal.

units.la: In pulmonis tumoribus:
units.tr: In tumours of the lung:

units.la: Inæquales.
units.tr: unequal.

units.la: Pleuritidis exitialis signum:
units.tr: Sign of deadly pleurisy:

units.la: Pulsus valde durus, parvus etiam, et ob hæc, caloremque creberrimus.
units.tr: The pulse is very hard and also small, and on account of these and the heat, very frequent.

units.la: Iecinore affecto qui pulsus:
units.tr: The pulses when the liver is affected:

units.la: Pulsus ex intemperie tumoribusque præter naturam prædictis consentiunt: sed minus ex ipsius inflammationibus indurescunt, quàm ex inflammationibus thoracis: & tantò qui dem, quàm ex pulmonis magis.
units.tr: The pulses agree with the intemperature and with the tumours that are contrary to nature; but they harden less from inflammations of the liver itself than from inflammations of the chest, and indeed by so much more than from those of the lung.

units.la: Iecinoris, ex tumore nunquam:
units.tr: Of the liver, from a tumour, never:

units.la: Mollis pulsus: sicut neque thoracis, quòd nunquâ in his nascatur œdema pituitosum. Compacta enim hæc membra, vt non eam admittant fluxionem, iecur item pituitam al terat facultate.
units.tr: a soft pulse, as also in the chest, because no watery oedema ever arises in these parts. For these members are compact, so that they do not admit such a fluxion, and the liver likewise alters the phlegm by its faculty.

units.la: Iecinoris, & lienis ex scirrho:
units.tr: Of liver and spleen, from scirrhus:

units.la: Pulsus valde duri.
units.tr: Pulses very hard.

units.la: Septo transuerso affecto qui pulsus.
units.tr: The pulse when the diaphragm is affected:

units.la: Si fluxione laboret, ea est,
units.tr: If it labours under a fluxion, it is

units.la: Vel flaua bilis:
units.tr: either yellow bile

units.la: Vel sanguinis calidi & tenuis. Nempe propter densitatem, neque crassum sanguinem, neque pituitam lentam vnquam recipit.
units.tr: or blood hot and thin. Namely, because of its density, it never receives thick blood or viscous phlegm.

units.la: Si igitur ea laboret, febricitetque,
units.tr: If therefore it labours under that and there is fever,

units.la: Pulsus insigniter durus paruusque: atque ob ambo hæc & copiam caloris, creberrimus.
units.tr: the pulse is remarkably hard and small, and on account of both these and the abundance of heat, very frequent.

units.la: Tensionem enim nulla alia pars ita arteriis infert, præsertim si pars neruosa adfecta sit: id quod & pleuritibus accidit, tum quòd tunica multos habeat neruos, tum quòd septo transuerso adhæreat.
units.tr: For no other part inflicts such tension on the arteries, especially if the nervous part is affected. This also happens in pleurisies, both because the membrane has many nerves and because it adheres to the diaphragm.

units.la: Si afficiatur citra febrem,
units.tr: If it is affected without fever:

units.la: Durus, paruus, non tamen multò crebrior: sed vel parum, vel nullo pacto.
units.tr: hard and small, yet not much more frequent, but either slightly or not at all.

units.la: Ventriculo intemperie affecto,
units.tr: Stomach affected by intemperature:

units.la: Similes prædictis.
units.tr: similar to the above.

units.la: Tumore, secundum fundum:
units.tr: By tumour, according to the base:

units.la: Non dissimiles prædictis ex tumore.
units.tr: Not unlike the above, from tumour.

units.la: Os uentris si tumore affectum:
units.tr: If the mouth of the stomach is affected by a tumour:

units.la: Durior, ob neruorum multitudinem: nō ta men ita durus, vt ex septo transuerso. Ventri culi siquidem molles sunt nerui, insignis sensus, & carnosa corporis substantia.
units.tr: harder, because of the multitude of nerves; yet not so hard as from the diaphragm. For the nerves of the stomach are soft, of keen sensation, and the substance of the body is fleshy.

units.la: Nerui vero septi transuersi, vt corpora ip sa, duri sunt & contenti.
units.tr: But the nerves of the diaphragm, like the bodies themselves, are hard and taut.

units.la: Si facultas materiæ copia degrauata, aut aliàs debilitata,
units.tr: If the faculty is weighed down by an abundance of matter, or otherwise weakened:

units.la: Languidi pulsus, parui, crebriqúe, & interdum inæquales, tum in his tribus, tū in celeri tate & tarditate.
units.tr: Languid pulses, small, frequent, and sometimes irregular, in these three respects, and in speed and slowness.

units.la: Vesica inflammata,
units.tr: Bladder inflamed:

units.la: Durior pulsus: durior siquidem, & neruosior est vesica.
units.tr: Pulse harder, for the bladder is harder and more sinewy.

units.la: Vtero inflammato,
units.tr: Uterus inflamed:

units.la: Non ita durus: sed citius quàm vesicæ cōuertuntur in alias differentias propter maiores, tum venas, tum arterias, & multò prius vtero, quàm vesicæ insertas.
units.tr: not so hard, but changes more quickly into other differences, because its veins and arteries are larger, and because they are inserted into the uterus much earlier than into the bladder.

units.la: CEREBRO affecto qui pulsus.
units.tr: The pulse when the BRAIN is affected:

units.la: Calido citra siccitatem in statu quidem arteriæ: Moderati & natiuis similes: sed magnitudine, celeritate, et crebritate tantū excedētes, quantum natiua superat morbosa caliditas.
units.tr: Warm without dryness, in the state of the artery: moderate and similar to natural ones, but exceeding them in size, speed and frequency as far as morbid heat exceeds natural heat.

units.la: Calidiore & ficciore, in quem affectu accedit membrana tenuis, & cuncti alij nerui: Duriores.
units.tr: Hotter and drier, an affection in which the thin membrane and all the other nerves are involved: Harder.

units.la: Calidiore & ficciore ex biliosi humoris affluentia: Duriores adhuc, quod magis tendatur arteria.
units.tr: Hotter and drier, from an influx of bilious humour: harder still, because the artery is more stretched.

units.la: Ex affluentia sanguinis feruidi: Siccitas minor, & maior tensio validiorque, & tumor maior.
units.tr: From an influx of fervid blood: less dryness, greater and stronger tension, and greater swelling.

units.la: Cerebro humidiore: Molles.
units.tr: Brain moister: Soft.

units.la: Cum febrili calore, Mollis & magnus: est ea affectio Lethargus.
units.tr: With febrile heat, soft and large: this affection is lethargy.

units.la: Cum pituita putrida, Molles item: & contenta arteriae specie praebentes: erit & haec affectio Lethargus.
units.tr: With putrid phlegm, likewise soft, and presenting the appearance of a contained artery: this affection too will be lethargy.

units.la: Ex bile & pituita affecto: Pulsus ambigunt.
units.tr: From bile and phlegm affecting it: the pulses are doubtful.

units.la: Cerebro frigiditate morbosa affecto citra materiam: Tardiores aequo, & rariores.
units.tr: Brain affected by morbid coldness without matter: slower than normal, and rarer.

units.la: Cum materia, & praesertim melancholica, Duriores.
units.tr: With matter, and especially melancholic matter, harder.

units.la: Cum pituitosa, quae crassa sit & glutinosa, Intenti. Cum humida & flatuosa:Molles sine tensione.
units.tr: With phlegmatic matter that is thick and glutinous, tense. With moist and flatulent matter: soft, without tension.

units.la: Ex confusa materia,Molles, & nonnihil intenti.
units.tr: From confused matter: soft, and somewhat tense.

units.la: MENYNGIBVS affectis qui pulsus.
units.tr: The pulse in affections of the meninges.

units.la: Menynx subtilis statim affectum suũ cerebro impartitur: sicut cerebrum, ipsi.
units.tr: The fine meninx immediately communicates its affection to the brain, and the brain likewise to it.

units.la: Dura menynx, quòd longè à cerebro sita sit, sola affici potest.
units.tr: The dura mater, because it lies far from the brain, can be affected alone.

units.la: Huius affectus, si insignis sit, cor ad consensionem solicitat, & arterias.
units.tr: If this affection is marked, it urges the heart and the arteries into sympathy.

units.la: Calidi affectus, vsum augent.
units.tr: Hot affections increase the activity of the pulse.

units.la: Frigidi, remittunt, & arterias indurant, praesertim corde altiores.
units.tr: Cold ones relax it and harden the arteries, especially those lying higher than the heart.

units.la: Sicci, intentũ & durum pulsum reddũt.
units.tr: Dry ones make the pulse tense and hard.

units.la: Humidi, mollem.
units.tr: Moist ones make it soft.

units.la: Partium igitur natura, in his omnibus accurate perpendenda.
units.tr: The nature of the parts must therefore be carefully weighed in all these cases.

units.la: Nempe corpora per se dura duris affecta morbis, maximam contrahunt duritiem:
units.tr: For bodies that are hard by nature, when affected by hard diseases, contract the greatest hardness.

units.la: Mollia mollibus affecta, magis emollescunt.
units.tr: Soft bodies affected by soft diseases become softer still.

units.la: Dura si humectantibus afficiantur, & mollia indurantibus, non extremum contrarÿ assequentur.
units.tr: If hard parts are affected by moistening agents, and soft parts by hardening ones, they do not reach the extreme of the contrary.

units.la: Hac ratione,
units.tr: On this principle:

units.la: Pulmonibus, & cerebro inflammatis, pul-sus non erit ita durus, sicut ex menyngibus.
units.tr: In inflamed lungs and brain, the pulse will not be as hard as it is in the meninges.

units.la: Ita de alis & inguinibus dicendum: sunt e-nim in ipsis quædam duriora & densiora: ali-qua rariora et molliora. atq; hæc pluribus et maioribus, illa paucioribus minoribusq; va-sis & neruis sunt prædita.
units.tr: The same must be said of the armpits and groins: for in them some parts are harder and denser, others rarer and softer; and the former are furnished with more and larger vessels and nerves, the latter with fewer and smaller ones.

units.la: TESTIBVS affectis, qui pulsus.
units.tr: The pulse in affections of the testicles.

units.la: Erythroide tunica peritonæo adnata, si in-flammetur,
units.tr: If the erythroid tunic, attached to the peritoneum, is inflamed:

units.la: Pulsus durus, & proinde minor.
units.tr: The pulse is hard, and therefore small.

units.la: Testibus inflammatis:
units.tr: When the testicles are inflamed:

units.la: Non ita durus, sed magnus causa febris. Nempe partes arteriosæ & venosæ, maiores habent pulsus:
units.tr: The pulse is not so hard, but large, and is the cause of fever. For arterial and venous parts have larger pulses;

units.la: Neruosæ autem, aut omnino nihil, aut paruos.
units.tr: nervous parts, however, have either none at all or small ones.

units.la: Iudicationibus quinam pulsus peculiares:
units.tr: Which pulses are peculiar to crises:

units.la: Altus, ut & vehemens omnium excre-tionum signa existunt, & stabile indicium morbi iudicium adesse.
units.tr: A high pulse, as well as a vehement one, are signs of all excretions, and a stable indication that a crisis is at hand.

units.la: Vehemens, & magnus precedente ine-qualitate, externam excretionem annunci-at: at:non præcedente inæqualitate, non semper portendit.
units.tr: A vehement and large pulse, with prior inequality, announces an external excretion; without prior inequality it does not always portend one.

units.la: Altus, semper portendit: si remota sit inæqualitas, modicam: copiosam, si multas sequitur inæqualitates, facultatemque copia onerari:
units.tr: A high pulse always portends it: if the inequality is remote, a moderate excretion; a copious one if many inequalities follow, and the faculty is burdened by the abundance.

units.la: Magnus & vndosus, ac veluti emollescens corpore rorido, sudores ostendit:
units.tr: A large and undulating pulse, and one that seems to soften, as with a dewy body, shows sweats.

units.la: Durus, vomitus magis quàm sudores:
units.tr: A hard pulse shows vomiting rather than sweats.

units.la: Magnus motum ad exteriora.
units.tr: A large pulse shows motion toward the exterior.

units.la: Inæqualis, in pluribus fieri solet iudicatio nibus, cùm non fiunt sine periculo & pugna, magisq; cùm ad ventriculum biliosi confluunt humores.
units.tr: Unequal pulses: crises usually occur in many cases, since they do not come without danger and struggle, and especially when bilious humours flow together into the stomach.

units.la: Excretiones simpliciter malæ, quæ pulsum magnum non habent, & celerem in contractione.
units.tr: Excretions that are simply bad are those that do not have a large pulse, and that are quick in contraction.

units.la: Vehementes, plures, & magni post inæquales, in morbo pituitosiore, iudicationem per abscessum indicant: maximè si diuturnus fuerit, & cætera frigida consentiant: vt hyems, regio, temperamentum, & similia.
units.tr: Vehement, numerous and large pulses after unequal ones, in a more phlegmatic disease, indicate a crisis by abscess: especially if the disease is long-lasting and other cold conditions agree, such as winter, the region, the temperament and the like.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: The end.

units.la: DE IVDICIIS VRINARVM TRACTATVS, EX PROBATIS COLLECTVS AVTHORIBVS, &in tabulæ formam confectus, adiectis etiam causis, quæ hanc vel illam urinã reddant:
units.tr: A TREATISE ON THE JUDGEMENTS OF URINES, COLLECTED FROM APPROVED AUTHORS AND DRAWN UP IN THE FORM OF A TABLE, with the causes also added which render this or that urine:

units.la: Ioanne Vassæo Meldensi authore.
units.tr: By John Vassaeus of Meaux, author.

units.la: F
units.tr: F

units.la: DE IVDICIIS VRINARVM TRACTATVS, EX probatis collectus authoribus, & in tabulae formam confectus.
units.tr: On the Judgements of Urine: a treatise gathered from approved authors and arranged in the form of a table.

units.la: CVM tres genere facultates in tribus existant principijs, cerebro, corde, & hepate: ex singulorum functionibus, tum imbecillitas tum robur dignoscuntur. Cerebri quidem memoria & ratiocinatione, & subseruientibus alijs arbitrarijs functionibus. Cordis, per arteriarum motus. Hepatis verò facultas, cuiusnam roboris vel imbecillitatis fuerit: hæc quidem quæ in ventre est, per ea quæ subeunt & subducuntur, agnoscitur: illa vero quæ in hepate & venis est, per vrinas. Sunt siquidem in huiusmodi vrinis signa euidentissima, alia siquidem exquisitæ concoctionis, alia diminutæ, alia verò prorsus abolitæ, veluti & in ventre contingit. Præterea et vt in ventre externa quædam pariter excernuntur cernuntur, quæ affectiones alias ostendunt: ita & ex vrinis affectus non contemnendi ostenduntur, quanquàm non omnes: neque enim morborum musculos infestantium secura est per vrinas significatio, imò parua: sicut tineæ voluuli, neque affectuum thoracis & pulmonum. Sunt tamen & in huiusmodi affectibus inspiciendæ: nam si bonæ sint, multum valent ad salutem: contrà si praue, amplificant simul ægri periculum, vt ex tertij epidemiorum commentarijs constat. Est autem vrina serum humorum invenis contentorum, ex eisdem commentarijs.
units.tr: Since the three faculties exist in three principles, the brain, the heart and the liver, their strength or weakness is recognised from the functions of each. Of the brain, by memory and reasoning, and by the voluntary functions that serve them. Of the heart, by the movement of the arteries. Of the liver, the faculty, whether strong or weak, is recognised: that which is in the stomach, by what goes in and out; but that which is in the liver and veins, by the urine. For in such urines there are very clear signs: some of exquisite concoction, others of diminished, others altogether abolished, just as also happens in the stomach. Moreover, just as certain external matters are likewise excreted in the stomach, which show other affections, so also from the urine affections not to be despised are shown, though not all: for the indication by urine is not reliable in diseases that attack the muscles, but is slight, as with ringworm and the like, nor in affections of the chest and lungs. Yet these must be examined in such affections too: for if the urine is good, it counts for much towards health; on the contrary, if bad, it increases the patient's danger at the same time, as is clear from the commentaries on the third book of the Epidemics. The urine is the serum of the humours contained in the body, according to the same commentaries.

units.la: COLLECTIO.
units.tr: COLLECTION.

units.la: Colligatur absoluta concoctione, Non seruetur vltra sex horas, vel vnam, teste Auicenna. Tota recipiatur & non pars. Non pronuncietur de ea nisi in matella resederit.
units.tr: Let the urine be collected once concoction is complete. It is not to be kept longer than six hours, or one, according to Avicenna. The whole should be taken, not a part. Nothing should be pronounced on it unless it has settled in the urinal.

units.la: Primum & quartum dicta sunt propter cotenta, quæ superflua quædam sunt tertiæ coctionis, de quibus iudicium fieri oportet. Secundum, quoniam tunc significatio minus efficax, color mutatur, & hypostasis dissoluitur, mutatur, aut densior reddita. Tertium, ut perfecta fiat cognitio.
units.tr: The first and fourth points have been stated because of the contents, which are certain superfluous matters of the third concoction, about which a judgement must be made. The second, because then the significance is less effective: the colour changes, and the sediment dissolves, or becomes denser. The third, so that a complete knowledge may be obtained.

units.la: IVDICIA QVAE impediunt.
units.tr: JUDGEMENTS WHICH HINDER.

units.la: Motatio vehemens, Locus obscurus, Locus nimis lucidus, Matula viridis, inferne lata vel arcta nimis, Radij solares, Frigus, Ventus, Cibus, Potio, Medicamentum, Exercitatio, Ieiunium, Vigiliae, Labor, Ira, Timor, Coitus, Vomitus, Euacuatio.
units.tr: Violent motion; a dark place; a place too bright; a green flask; a flask too wide or too narrow at the base; rays of the sun; cold; wind; food; drink; medicine; exercise; fasting; wakefulness; labour; anger; fear; coitus; vomiting; evacuation.

units.la: Primum dictum est, ne multa in eis transponantur: bullae enim rumpuntur & transportantur, contenta ex proprijs abscedunt locis. Secundum, quoniam loci umbratiles, non parum de coloribus tollunt. Tertium, & quintum, quoniam lucescentia multa colores redduntur remissores.
units.tr: The first has been stated so that many things are not shifted about in them: for the bubbles are broken and carried across, and the contents break away from their proper places. The second, because shaded places take away much of the colours. The third and fifth, because in bright light many colours appear fainter.

units.la: Quartum, quoniam si uiridis, & coloribus aliquid aufert, & urinarum substantiam minuit: quinetiam in talibus contenta non exacte repraesentantur, si inferne lata uel arcta nimis, quem locum contenta obtinere debeant, non dignoscetur. Sextum, & septimum, ne uento perturbetur, & frigore congeletur, donec separatio fiat. Octauum, nempe cibi corpori oblati si non recte transmutantur, aut non probe in sanguinem mutantur, similem sibi urinam efficient: cuiusmodi sunt olera. Nonum patet, nam si aquam aut uinum albu abunde hauserimus, alba & aquosa apparebit urina: sin crassum & nigrum, crassior nigriorum; urina erit: quem admodum flaua, ubi uinum uetus flauumque; biberimus. Decimum constat ex rheo barbaro adsumpto: nam mox in urina eius apperet color: ite ex calsia fistulosa. Vndecimum, duodecimum, decimumtertium, decimumquartum, decimumquintum, & decimumsextum constant, quoniam haec omnia urinas tingant. Decimumseptimum item, quod coitus urinam pinguiorem reddat. Vomitus item & euacuatio colores urinarum mutat, & substantias.
units.tr: The fourth, because if the flask is green, it takes something from the colours and diminishes the substance of the urines; moreover, in such flasks the contents are not represented exactly, and if the flask is too wide or too narrow at the base, one cannot tell what place the contents ought to occupy. The sixth and seventh, lest it be disturbed by wind and congealed by cold before separation takes place. The eighth, namely that food offered to the body, if it is not properly transformed or not well changed into blood, will produce a urine like itself: such are vegetables. The ninth is obvious: for if we have drunk plenty of water or white wine, the urine will appear white and watery; but if thick and dark wine, the urine will be thicker and darker, just as it is yellow when we drink old yellow wine. The tenth is established from rhubarb taken: for at once its colour appears in the urine; likewise from hollow cassia. The eleventh, twelfth, thirteenth, fourteenth, fifteenth and sixteenth are established, because all these tinge the urines. The seventeenth likewise: coitus makes the urine richer. Vomiting likewise, and evacuation, change the colours and substances of the urines.

units.la: VRINAE DIIVDICANTVR.
units.tr: URINE IS JUDGED (the diagnosis of urine).

units.la: Substantia, Quantitate, Perspicuitate, Colore, Odore, Meiendi modo, Contentis. Substantia triplex, Tenuis, Crassa, Mediocris. Quantitas triplex, Multa, Pauca, Mediocris. Perspicuitas triplex, Translucida, Turbulenta, Mediocris. Color multiplex, Albus Intense, Remisse, Intense: Crystalleus, Aqueus. Remisse: Lacteus, Glaucus, Charopus. Colores alij, prout album sequuntur. Subspiceus, Spiceus, Subaureus, Aureus, Subcroceus, Croceus, Rufus, id est, rutilus, igneus vel flammeus, Subrubens, Rubens, Prærubens, Vineus, Passeus, Viridis, Venetus, Liuidus, Niger.
units.tr: Substance, Quantity, Clarity, Colour, Smell, Manner of Urinating, Contents. Substance is threefold: thin, thick, or moderate. Quantity is threefold: much, little, or moderate. Clarity is threefold: transparent, turbid, or moderate. Colour is manifold: white, which is intense or remiss; intense: crystalline, watery. Remiss: milky, glaucous (sea-green), charopus (greyish-yellow). Other colours follow in the wake of white: subspiceus (somewhat spice-coloured), spiceus, subaureus (somewhat golden), aureus (golden), subcroceus (somewhat saffron), croceus (saffron), rufus, that is, ruddy, fiery or flame-coloured, subrubens (somewhat red), rubens (red), prærubens (over-red), vineus (wine-coloured), passeus (raisin-coloured), viridis (green), venetus (blue-grey), liuidus (livid), niger (black).

units.la: Meiendi modus multiplex,
units.tr: The manner of urinating is manifold,

units.la: Difficilis, Facilis, Mediocris, Voluntarius, Inuoluntarius, Cum dolore, Absque dolore.
units.tr: Difficult, easy, moderate, voluntary, involuntary, with pain, without pain.

units.la: Contenta,
units.tr: The contents,

units.la: Hypostasis, Enæorema, Nubes, Bulla, Frustula, Ramenta, Circulus, Spuma, Pinguedo, Pus, Arena, Calculi, Phlegmata, Thrombi sanguinis, Pili, Squamma, Genitura.
units.tr: Sediment (hypostasis), enaeorema, clouds, bubbles, small fragments, scrapings, rings, foam, fat, pus, sand, stones, phlegm, clots of blood, hairs, scales, semen.

units.la: NOMINVM COLORVM explicatio.
units.tr: Explanation of the names of the colours.

units.la: Albus crystalleus, crystallo similis.
units.tr: White, like crystal.

units.la: Albus aqueus, aquæ similis.
units.tr: White, watery, like water.

units.la: Albus lacteus, lacti similis.
units.tr: White, milky, like milk.

units.la: Albus glaucus, veluti cornu pellucidum.
units.tr: White, glaucous, like translucent horn.

units.la: Albus charopus, pilis subalbidis cameli similis vel ungui lapillo. Charopus tamen apud Galenum oculis leonis similis dicitur.
units.tr: White, charopus, like the whitish hair of a camel or like a pale pebble. Galen, however, says that charopus is like the eyes of a lion.

units.la: Subspiceus fit, si parum spicei humoris succo claro, ut aqua est, mieceris.
units.tr: It becomes subspiceus if you mix a little spicy humour with clear juice, which is like water.

units.la: Spiceus, si plus addideris.
units.tr: Spiceus, if you add more.

units.la: Subaureus, qui non puro auro similis.
units.tr: Subaureus, which is like impure gold.

units.la: Aureus, qui puro auro.
units.tr: Aureus, which is like pure gold.

units.la: Subcroceus, qui aquam repraesentat, in qua dissolutus sit flos carthami.
units.tr: Subcroceus, which resembles water in which safflower has been dissolved.

units.la: Croceus, in qua flos croci.
units.tr: Croceus, in which there is saffron flower.

units.la: Rufus, cum flaua bilis exuperans, uel syncera urinae mixta sit.
units.tr: Reddish, when yellow bile predominates or is mixed with clear urine.

units.la: Subrubens, bolo armeno similis.
units.tr: Subrubens, like Armenian bole.

units.la: Rubens & puniceus, pomis quae rubrum colorem praese ferunt, ut sunt cerussa.
units.tr: Red and purple, like the fruits that show a red colour, such as cherries.

units.la: Vineus, qui uino nigro similis est, aut hepatis colori.
units.tr: Vinous, which is like black wine or the colour of the liver.

units.la: Passeus, uino cocto similis.
units.tr: Passeus, like cooked wine.

units.la: Venetus, seu fuscus, qui ex puro albo & nigro aequaliter cofusis gignitur, qui modo brunus, mo do blauus uulgo dicitur.
units.tr: Venetus, or fuscus (brown), which arises from pure white and black mixed in equal parts; in common speech it is called now brown, now blue.

units.la: Liuidus, plumbeus est.
units.tr: Livid is leaden.

units.la: Niger notus.
units.tr: Black is well known.

units.la: Viridis, uia est ad nigrum.
units.tr: Green is a step towards black.

units.la: VRINA OPTIMA, ALIARVM omnium regula & amussis, quae in viris temperatis, & aetate florentibus reperitur.
units.tr: THE BEST URINE, the rule and standard of all others, which is found in men of temperate constitution and in the prime of life.

units.la: a. Colore subaurea vel subcrocea.
units.tr: a. Colour golden or saffron-yellow.

units.la: Substantia inter tenuem, ut aqua: & crassam, ut subinugalium lotium.
units.tr: Substance between thin, like water, and thick, like the urine of those who have been rubbed with oil.

units.la: c. Proportione potui respondens.
units.tr: c. In proportion corresponding to the drink.

units.la: d. Matula non adhaerens.
units.tr: d. Not adhering to the flask.

units.la: e. Cum hypostasi,
units.tr: e. With its sediment,

units.la: Alba, Laui, Aequali. f. Sine pilis, bullis, tuberculis, & aliis malignis contentis.
units.tr: White, clear, even. f. Without hairs, bubbles, tubercles, and other malignant contents.

units.la: Vrina omnis quouis modo ab hac declinet, ab optima cadit sanitate.
units.tr: Any urine that departs from this in any way falls short of the best health.

units.la: a. Primū constat: nam ubi mediocris atq; ut decet, concoctio fit, tum crocea atq; aurea bilis generatur, & urinæ apparent subcroceæ atq; subaureæ, colore bilis remisso, ob mixtionem sereæ humiditatis, cuius color albus est. Secundū, nempe si cō coctio exacta fuerit, substantia apparet mediocris. Fitq; , cum genuina caliditas dominando cibo & potui comesis, atque humoribus internis, suapte natura concoctiones ut decet, efficit.
units.tr: a. The first is established thus: when digestion is moderate and as it should be, yellow and golden bile is generated, and the urines appear somewhat saffron and golden, the colour of the bile being softened by the mixing in of watery serous moisture, whose colour is white. Second, namely if the concoction has been complete, the substance appears moderate. And this comes about when the natural heat, mastering the food and drink taken in and the internal humours, brings about the concoctions as it should by its own nature.

units.la: c. Tertium dicitur: nam alterationem aliquam sa ctam esse in his quæ extrinsecus sunt, significat urina maior aut minor, siue multum excesserit, siue multum recesserit.
units.tr: c. The third is stated thus: for the urine being greater or lesser, whether it has exceeded much or fallen much short, shows that some alteration has taken place in those things which are external.

units.la: d. Quartum: nam ita humor lentus & glutinosus esset.
units.tr: d. The fourth: for in this way the humour would be viscous and glutinous.

units.la: e. Quintum ostendit puris generatio, quòd puri proportionalem habeat hypostasis: ex Galeni commentario circa finem primi prognosticorum.
units.tr: e. The fifth is shown by the generation of pus, since the sediment bears a proportion to pus: from Galen's commentary near the end of the first book of the Prognostics.

units.la: f. Sextum ostendetur ex his quæ cum hypostasi apparent.
units.tr: f. The sixth will be shown from those things which appear together with the sediment.

units.la: VRINÆ ÆETATVM ET sexuum quales.
units.tr: Urine of the ages and sexes, and their qualities.

units.la: Senum,
units.tr: Of the old,

units.la: a. Albæ, b. Tenues, c. Cum Hypostasi pauca, & ad cruditatem declinante.
units.tr: a. White; b. thin; c. with little sediment, and inclined to crudity.

units.la: a. b.Primi & secundi causa est, quod senum ætas quantum procedat, tantum erga frigidum declinet, genuina marcescat caliditas, coctio diminuatur,& ab eminentia frigiditatis obscuretur.
units.tr: a. b. The cause of the first and second is that as the age of the old advances, so far does it tend towards cold; the native warmth withers, concoction is diminished, and the urine is darkened by the predominance of coldness.

units.la: c.Tertium efficit nutritio diminuta, propter im minutam senum potentiam.
units.tr: c. The third is produced by diminished nutrition, on account of the diminished power of the old.

units.la: Puerorum,
units.tr: Of children,

units.la: a. A subaureis & subcroceis parum recedentes,
units.tr: a. Departing little from the golden and saffron colours,

units.la: b. Substantia iuuenum vrinas parum excellente,
units.tr: b. with urine of substance somewhat exceeding that of young people,

units.la: c. Cumulata hypostasi.
units.tr: c. with a heaped-up sediment.

units.la: a.Primum contingit, quod puerorum calor naturalis multus sit, multa quoque naturalis humidi tas:hinc colores remissiores multa humiditate ma defcentes.
units.tr: a. The first occurs because children have much natural heat, and also much natural moisture; hence their colours are milder, being softened by much moisture.

units.la: b. Secundum, quod puerorum caliditas, iuuenū caliditatem potius quantitate superans, circa substantiam humorum producendam excelluit.
units.tr: b. The second, because the heat of children, surpassing the heat of young people more in quantity than in quality, is excellent in producing the substance of the humours.
