units.la: c. Tertium efficiunt, multa humorum elaboratio, multus esus,& nutritionis actio, quæ necessitati requirentium membrorum satisfaciat. Nam ca lori est opus materia,tum ad nutriendum, tum ad membrorum incrementum.
units.tr: c. The third is brought about by the great elaboration of humours, the abundant eating and the activity of nutrition, which satisfies the need of the growing limbs. For heat needs matter, both for nourishing and for the growth of the limbs.

units.la: Mulierum etiam temperatarum & ætate florentium.
units.tr: Of women also who are of a temperate constitution and flourishing in age.

units.la: a. Asubaureis & subcroceis non multum recedentes album versus,
units.tr: a. Not greatly departing from the golden and saffron colours towards white,

units.la: b. Substantia tenues,
units.tr: b. thin in substance,

units.la: c. Pluribus quam virorum contentis.
units.tr: c. containing more than that of men.

units.la: a. b. Primi, & secundi ratio est, quod genus muli ebre domesticum sit, paucis exercitijs utens, atque remissam habens naturalem caliditatem, uirili generi comparatum: & ob id debiles efficiat concoctiones, & a perfecta recedentes.
units.tr: a. b. The reason for the first and second is that the female sex is domestic, using few exercises, and having a relaxed natural heat compared with the male sex; and therefore it makes concoctions weak and departing from perfection.

units.la: c. Tertium fit ob naturalis humiditatis excessum, & superfluitatum abundantiam, quae oriuntur a debili concoctione.
units.tr: c. The third happens on account of an excess of natural moisture and an abundance of superfluities, which arise from weak concoction.

units.la: Vrinae eorum qui se plus iusto exercent.
units.tr: Urine of those who exercise themselves more than is right.

units.la: a. Ad aureum croceumque tendentes,
units.tr: a. Tending towards golden and saffron,

units.la: b. Contentis paucis, tenuibus, & interdum cum innatante liquamine.
units.tr: b. with few contents, thin, and sometimes with a floating oily film.

units.la: a. Primum fit, quod calore ob morum exaucto bileus humor ab intensa comburatur caliditate.
units.tr: a. The first happens because, with the heat increased by movement, the bilious humour is scorched by the intense heat.

units.la: b. Secundum ob feream humiditatem diminutam: & quoniam membra attenuantur caliditatis excessu, & disperduntur uaporificata sudoribus, uel alijs occultis spirationibus, decens est ut & exauctis exercitijs aliqua in urinis appareant innatantia colliquamina, aliquo pingui colliquefacto, uel a renibus, uel a partibus alijs.
units.tr: b. The second, because the watery moisture is diminished; and since the limbs are thinned by excess of heat, and are wasted by vaporising sweats or other hidden exhalations, it is fitting that, when exercises are increased, some floating oily films should appear in the urine, some fatty matter being liquefied either from the kidneys or from other parts.

units.la: Vrinae ociosam & inertem vitam viuentium.
units.tr: Urine of those who live an idle and inactive life.

units.la: a. Ad album vergentes,
units.tr: a. Tending towards white,

units.la: b. Contentis multis & crudioribus.
units.tr: b. with many contents, and rather crude.

units.la: a. Primum accidit ob paucitatem calidi motionem habentis, marcescentisq; motionis uacationem: id quod ostenduit ligna rogis congesta abunde, non uentilata.
units.tr: a. The first occurs because of the scarcity of heat, which has little motion, and the absence of withering motion: as is shown by logs heaped up in great quantity on pyres, which are not ventilated.

units.la: b Secundum accidit quod caliditate non mota, tabescente, frustretur adeptio perfectæ concoctionis.
units.tr: b. The second occurs because, when the heat is not stirred up and is wasting away, the attainment of perfect concoction is thwarted.

units.la: IVDICIVM VRINARVM SECUNDVM anni tempora.
units.tr: JUDGMENT OF URINES ACCORDING TO THE SEASONS OF THE YEAR.

units.la: Vere ineunte,
units.tr: At the beginning of spring,

units.la: a. Albæ & subspiceæ,
units.tr: a. White and pale straw-coloured,

units.la: b. Quantitate maiores,
units.tr: b. Greater in quantity,

units.la: c. Contentis pluribus, crassioribus, & crudioribus.
units.tr: c. With more contents, thicker and cruder.

units.la: a. Albæ & subspiceæ, quod uicta ob frigoris adhuc dominantis ambitum caliditate, defectus coctionis accidant, tam in colore quam substantia.
units.tr: a. White and pale straw-coloured, because, the heat being overcome by the surrounding cold which still prevails, defects of concoction occur, both in colour and in substance.

units.la: b. Quantitate autem maiores, humiditate scilicet humorum in corpore per totam hyemem collecta.
units.tr: b. Greater in quantity, namely because of the humidity of the humours collected in the body through the whole winter.

units.la: c. Contentis uero pluribus, ob plures comesorum multorum superfluitates. Crassioribus item & crudioribus, ob easdem causas.
units.tr: c. More contents, indeed, because of the excess residues of the many foods eaten. Thicker and cruder likewise, for the same reasons.

units.la: Cum procedit,
units.tr: As it advances,

units.la: A subspiceis & spiceis ad subaureas & sub croceas, Substantia æquales,
units.tr: From pale-straw and straw-coloured to golden and saffron-coloured, in substance equal,

units.la: Contentis mediocribus.
units.tr: with moderate contents.

units.la: Nempe temperata existente qualitate, omnia ad mediocritatem reducuntur.
units.tr: Namely, since the quality is tempered, everything is brought back to moderation.

units.la: Æstate, cùm incipit,
units.tr: In summer, when it begins,

units.la: a. Subaureæ & subcroceæ, b. Substantia tenuiores, Hypostasi quàm mediocris Tenuiore, sed { Alba, Lœui, & Æquali.
units.tr: a. Golden and saffron-coloured, b. thinner in substance, thinner than moderate in sediment, but white, smooth, and even.

units.la: a. Subaureæ, subcroceæ, quòd calore liberè in toto corpore diffuso, atque præsenti materiæ dominante, concoctioneque facta ut decet, urinæ fiant mediocres.
units.tr: a. Golden and saffron-coloured, since the heat, diffused freely through the whole body and dominating the matter present, and the concoction being made as it should be, the urines become moderate.

units.la: b. Sed substantia & contentis tenuioribus, quòd principales partes tenuentur atque disperdantur aëris caliditate.
units.tr: b. But thinner in substance and contents, because the principal parts are thinned and destroyed by the heat of the air.

units.la: Cùm viget æstas,
units.tr: When summer is at its height,

units.la: a. Aureæ & croceæ, b. Substantia tenuiores, c. Minores quantitate, d. Contentis paucis & tenuibus, & quodam modo albis.
units.tr: a. Golden and saffron-coloured, b. thinner in substance, c. smaller in quantity, d. with few and thin contents, and in a certain way white.

units.la: d. Aureæ
units.tr: d. Golden

units.la: a. Aureæ & croceæ, ob adauctam ex aëre æstuante bilem.
units.tr: a. Golden and saffron-coloured, because bile is increased by the seething air.

units.la: b. Substantia tenuiores, ob concoctiones secun dum naturam diminutas, calore naturali à calore nos ambiente disperdito.
units.tr: b. Thinner in substance, because the concoctions are diminished contrary to nature, the natural heat being dispersed by the heat surrounding us.

units.la: c. Minores quantitate, partim dissoluta in sudores materia, partim disperdita per occultas euapo-rationes.
units.tr: c. Smaller in quantity, partly because matter is dissolved into sweats, partly because it is lost through hidden evaporations.

units.la: d. Contentis paucis & tenuibus & quodam modo albis, quòd disperdatur, & tenuetur materia, at-que coctiones debiliores fiant.
units.tr: d. Few and thin contents, and in a certain way white, because the matter is dispersed and thinned, and the concoctions become weaker.

units.la: Autumno, cùm accessit,
units.tr: In autumn, when it arrives,

units.la: a. Ad mediocritatem concedentes, b. Tenues & pellucidæ, c. Paucæ. d. Contentis paucis, sed Albis, Lœuibus, & æqualibus.
units.tr: a. Tending towards moderation, b. thin and clear, c. few. d. With few contents, but white, smooth, and even.

units.la: a. Ad mediocritatem concedentes, calore scili-cet uehementer diminuto.
units.tr: a. Tending towards moderation, namely with the heat greatly diminished.

units.la: b. c. d. Tenues, pellucidæ, & paucæ tum urinæ, tum hypostases, ob præstantem siccitatem.
units.tr: b. c. d. Thin, clear, and few, both urines and sediments, because of their outstanding dryness.

units.la: Cùm procedit, Mediocria omnia.
units.tr: As it advances, all moderate.

units.la: Quòd coctiones meliores fiant, caliditate genui-na ob frigidos uentos uires resumente, & tempera-mento coctionibus adlato omnibus. Hyeme, cùm incipit, a. Ad album vergentes, Substantia tenues, c. Contentis pluribus, & fortasse mediocribus.
units.tr: Because the concoctions become better, the natural heat regaining its strength from the cold winds, and a temperament being brought to all the concoctions. In winter, when it begins: a. tending towards white and thin in substance; c. with more contents, and perhaps moderate.

units.la: a. Ad album uergentes & tenues, alterata scilicet quodam modo ob aêrem frigidiorem interna caliditate, atq; increscente pituiteo humore.
units.tr: a. Tending towards white and thin, namely altered in a certain way by the colder air through the internal heat, and with the phlegmatic humour increasing.

units.la: c. Contentis verò pluribus, ob sumptiones ciborum ampliores & coctiones ualidiores, calore scilicet roborato, iuuantibusq; somnis longioribus.
units.tr: c. With more contents, indeed, because of larger intakes of food and stronger concoctions, namely the heat being strengthened, and longer sleeps helping.

units.la: Cùm procedit,
units.tr: As it advances,

units.la: a. Albæ, Quantitate maiores, c. Substantijs differentes, d. Contentis pluribus & crudioribus.
units.tr: a. White, greater in quantity; c. differing in substance; d. with more and cruder contents.

units.la: a. Albæ quidem, quòd genuina caliditas à frigore aëris exaucto læsa sit, bileusq; humor prorsus tabescant.
units.tr: a. White indeed, because the natural heat, impaired by the cold of the air, is weakened, and the bilious humour wholly wastes away.

units.la: c. Substantijs differentes, nam modo tenues propter imperfectam concoctionem, ob frigiditatis aëris præstantiâ: modò crassæ & conturbatæ ob crudum, qui hoc tempore uigat humorem.
units.tr: c. Differing in substance: sometimes thin, because of imperfect concoction, owing to the prevalence of the cold air; sometimes thick and turbid, because of the raw humour which flourishes at this season.

units.la: d. Contentis pluribus & crudioribus, quòd genuina caliditas domare non possit comesa multa, uel quòd multa elaborata sint, multa apparet. Cruda quoque & crasiora, aut frigiditate genuinam caliditatem tabefaciente, aut quòd plura sumpta sint, quàm natura proficere possit.
units.tr: d. More and cruder contents, because the natural heat cannot subdue the large amount eaten, or because much appears not to have been worked up. Also raw and thicker, either because the cold wastes the natural heat, or because more has been taken than nature can deal with.

units.la: VRINARVM IVDICIA EX simplicibus intemperaturis.
units.tr: THE JUDGEMENTS OF URINES FROM THE SIMPLE INTEMPERATURES.

units.la: Caliditas si exaucta,
units.tr: If heat prevails,

units.la: a. Aureæ & croceæ, b. Substantia mediocritatem excedente, cum splendore quodam, c. Contentis mediocribus, sed naturalem albedinem diffugientibus,
units.tr: a. Golden and saffron-coloured; b. Substance exceeding the mean, with a certain brightness; c. Contents moderate, but departing from natural whiteness.

units.la: a Aureæ & croceæ, ob bilem acutiorem effectā, humiditatemq; ablatam.
units.tr: a. Golden and saffron-coloured, because the bile has become sharper and the moisture has been removed.

units.la: b. Substantia mediocritatem excedente, quòd substantia à mediocribus discedant: cum quodam splendore, quòd exaucto acumine quod humiditatem asperante consumit, splendor conspectetur.
units.tr: b. Substance exceeding the mean, because the substances depart from the moderate ones; with a certain brightness, because when the sharpness has been heightened, it consumes the moisture that roughens, and brightness is seen.

units.la: c. Naturalem albedinem diffugientibus, quòd tinctura quædam ab excessu bilis distributa coloret contenta ipsa.
units.tr: c. Departing from natural whiteness, because a certain tinge, spread from the excess of bile, colours the contents themselves.

units.la: Frigiditas quantum intenditur,
units.tr: As cold is intensified,

units.la: a. Tantundem albescunt vrinæ, b. Substantia crassiore, c. Contentis minoribus & crudaceis, & interdum crassescunt vniuersæ &conturbantur.
units.tr: a. The urines become equally white; b. Substance thicker; c. Contents smaller and somewhat crude; and sometimes all of them thicken and are disturbed.

units.la: a. Quòd tantundem albescant urinæ, quantum intendatur frigiditas, facit quòd humor croceus proprium colorem nactus nō fit, capiens spiceum vel subspiceum secundum mensuram imperfectæ concoctionis.
units.tr: a. The urines become equally white as cold is intensified, because the yellow humour, not gaining its proper colour, takes on a straw colour or near-straw colour, according to the degree of imperfect concoction.

units.la: b. Substantia crassiore, quòd non facile à genui na caliditate domita & concocta fit.
units.tr: b. Thicker substance, because it is not easily subdued and concocted by the natural heat.

units.la: c. Contentis minoribus, quòd diminuto calore etiam nutritio minor sit: crudis, ob caloris imbe-cillitatem. Conturbantur quoq; interdum & craf-fescunt, cruditate ob imbecillitatem uirtutis alte-rantis uincente. Nempe calore præstante, quæ te-nuia sunt crassescunt concocta: quæ uerò alia ratio ne crassa erant, hæc tenuantur. Tenues autem po-tius per intemperaturam fiunt: crassæ uerò per hu-morum cruditatem.
units.tr: c. Smaller contents, because with diminished heat even the nutritive heat is less; crude, because of the weakness of the heat. They are also sometimes disturbed and thicken, crudity prevailing through the weakness of the altering power. Indeed, when heat is effective, thin things thicken when concocted; and conversely, things that were otherwise thick are made thinner. Thin things, however, come about rather through intemperature; thick ones through crudity of the humours.

units.la: Humiditas si vincat,
units.tr: If moisture prevails,

units.la: a. Ad album vergentes,
units.tr: a. Tending to white,

units.la: b. Quantitate maiores,
units.tr: b. Greater in quantity,

units.la: c. Subtenues,
units.tr: c. Rather thin,

units.la: d. Contentis multis & crudis.
units.tr: d. Contents many and crude.

units.la: a.b. Ad album uergunt urinæ, & quantitate ma-iores fiunt, quòd humiditas excedens ut obtundat urinæ naturalem colorem, ita & quantitatem au-geat.
units.tr: a.b. The urines tend to white and become greater in quantity, because the excess moisture dulls the natural colour of the urine and likewise increases its quantity.

units.la: c. Subtenues, quæ mediocritatem substantiæ ef-fugiant.
units.tr: c. Rather thin, because they fall short of the moderate substance.

units.la: d. Contentis multis, ob multam elaborationē, quòd humidum facile nutriat: crudis, quòd humi-do existente multo imperfecta sit elaboratio.
units.tr: d. Contents many, because of much elaboration, since moisture readily nourishes; crude, because with moisture abundant the elaboration is much imperfect.

units.la: Siccitas si vincat,
units.tr: If dryness prevails,

units.la: a. Calore mediocris cum splendore,
units.tr: a. Colour moderate, with brightness,

units.la: b. Mediocres substantia,
units.tr: b. Moderate substance,

units.la: c. Quantitate minores,
units.tr: c. Smaller in quantity,

units.la: d. Contentis paucis atque exactè coctis.
units.tr: d. Contents few and exactly concocted.

units.la: a. Colore mediocres, praesertim si colorans humor nihil affectus sit: cum splendore, ob uigorem colorantis humoris.
units.tr: a. Colour moderate, especially if the colouring humour has not been affected at all; with brightness, because of the vigour of the colouring humour.

units.la: b. Mediocres substantia, praesertim si non intenduntur: intenduntur enim aliquando.
units.tr: b. Moderate substance, especially if they are not intensified; for they are sometimes intensified.

units.la: c. Quantitate minores, ob humiditatis paucitatem.
units.tr: c. Smaller in quantity, because of the scarcity of moisture.

units.la: d. Contentis paucis, cum pauca processerit in numerando humiditas: Exactè coctis, quòd facilè à caliditate sunt domita.
units.tr: d. Contents few, since the moisture is scanty in amount; exactly concocted, because they are easily subdued by heat.

units.la: VRINAE SECVNDVM REgiones & cibos, proportione his respondent.
units.tr: URINE ACCORDING TO REGIONS AND FOODS, CORRESPONDING TO THEM IN PROPORTION.

units.la: Somnolentorum, seu qui dormiuerunt non secundum naturam, id est, non ob suauem humiditatem & mediocrem natiuam caliditatem, sed ob humiditatem multâ praesertim pituiteam, atque ob comesa & medicamina frigida,
units.tr: Of those who are drowsy, or who have slept not according to nature, that is, not because of a pleasant moisture and moderate natural heat, but because of moisture, especially much phlegmatic moisture, and because of eaten foods and cold medicines,

units.la: Ad album vergentes,
units.tr: Tending towards white,

units.la: Substantia crassae aut subtenues,
units.tr: Of thick or thin substance,

units.la: Contentis pluribus & incoctis.
units.tr: With many and undigested contents.

units.la: Tria haec ex concoctionis contingunt defectu.
units.tr: These three arise from a defect of concoction.

units.la: Eorum qui secudum naturam dormiuerunt.
units.tr: Of those who have slept according to nature.

units.la: Spiceæ, Substantia mediocri, Contentis maioribus & bene coctis.
units.tr: Of good appearance, of moderate substance, with larger contents that are well concocted.

units.la: Trium horum rationes ex antecedentibus maximè patent.
units.tr: The reasons for these three are made fairly clear from what has gone before.

units.la: Eorum qui immoderatè vigilarunt ob causam aliquam,
units.tr: Of those who have stayed awake immoderately for some cause,

units.la: a. Tenues, b. Versicolores, Contentis extraneis magis.
units.tr: a. Thin, b. Varicoloured, with foreign contents in greater amount.

units.la: a. Tenues & aliquando albissimæ profluüt aut ob bilis regressum ad cerebrum, aut ob insaniæ speciem.
units.tr: a. Thin, and sometimes very white, flow either because of bile returning to the brain, or because of a semblance of madness.

units.la: b. Versicolores, nempe interdum albæ, interdū croceæ,& aureæ,ac oleaceæ,& nigræ, secundū cau sæ mutantis proprietatem.
units.tr: b. Varicoloured, namely sometimes white, sometimes saffron and golden, and olive-coloured, and black, according to the changing nature of the cause.

units.la: c. Contentis extraneis magis, nempe inæqualibus & maximè confusis, coctione non tam facile procedente,si aut aliqua intemperatura excesserit, aut usquequaq; homo uigilauerit.
units.tr: c. With foreign contents in greater amount, namely unequal and very confused, with concoction not proceeding so easily, if either some intemperance has occurred or the man has stayed awake altogether.

units.la: Multum comedentium, & non coquentium,
units.tr: Of those who eat much and do not digest,

units.la: Tenues, Albæ, Et interdum absque sedimento.
units.tr: Thin, white, and sometimes without sediment.

units.la: Hæc errorem à perfecta concoctione contigisse ostendunt.
units.tr: These show that the error arose from imperfect concoction.

units.la: Procrastinantium in cruditate, Substantia & contentis extraneæ.
units.tr: Of those who put off digestion in crudity: substance and contents foreign.

units.la: Ieiunantium,
units.tr: Of those who fast,

units.la: a. Flammeæ & croceæ,
units.tr: a. Flame-coloured and saffron,

units.la: b. Tenues,
units.tr: b. Thin,

units.la: c. Hypostasi minore.
units.tr: c. With a smaller sediment.

units.la: a. Flammeæ & croceæ ob calorem acutiorem de uorata humiditate redditum.
units.tr: a. Flame-coloured and saffron, owing to the sharper heat that has drawn back the consumed moisture.

units.la: b. Tenues ob illam calidi affectionem.
units.tr: b. Thin, owing to that affection of heat.

units.la: c. Hypostasi minore, quòd desint homini alimenta.
units.tr: c. With a smaller sediment, because the man lacks food.

units.la: Fame oppressorum,
units.tr: Of those oppressed by hunger,

units.la: Tenues,
units.tr: Thin,

units.la: Albæ,
units.tr: White,

units.la: Sine hypostasi.
units.tr: Without sediment.

units.la: Hæc fiunt concedente ad frigidum habitu ob caloris tabem.
units.tr: These occur when the body inclines to cold, owing to the wasting away of heat.

units.la: VRINARVM IVDICIA EX earum substantia.
units.tr: URINE JUDGMENTS FROM ITS SUBSTANCE.

units.la: Tenuis & subtilis,
units.tr: Thin and fine,

units.la: Lapsum caliditatis genuinæ,
units.tr: Indicates a lapse of natural heat,

units.la: b. Venarum, hepatis, renum, & vasorum vri-narium opilationem, c. Naturæ debilitatem,
units.tr: b. Obstruction of the veins, liver, kidneys and urinary vessels; c. Weakness of nature;

units.la: d. Canalium vrinæ læsam attractricem,
units.tr: d. Impaired attractive power of the urinary passages;

units.la: e. Frigiditatem vehementem cum siccitate,
units.tr: e. Intense cold with dryness,

units.la: Lapsum caliditatis genuinæ, aut superata ab aliqua potente frigiditate, aut quod extranea caliditas aliqua occasione præcedens eam occupauerit, ita vt ab actione propria prohibeatur: id quod patet in his quæ elixantur sub Sole vehementer radiante, & loco maximè frigido.
units.tr: A lapse of natural heat, either overcome by some powerful cold, or because some foreign heat, having arisen on some occasion, has occupied it so that it is prevented from its proper action. This is evident in things boiled under a very strongly shining sun, and in a very cold place.

units.la: b. Venarum, hepatis, &c. Nempe cum uel circa renes atque reliqua uasa urinaria, uel circa particulas aliquas quæ coërcere possunt, ut urinæ mediocres exeant, oppilatio aliqua non parua gignitur ab aliqua affectione, tum urina per angustias uelu ti per defæcatorium emuncta perquam tenuis exit, ut patet ex his qui uinum limosum & crassum colantes, pellucidissimum efficiant.
units.tr: b. Of the veins, liver, etc. Namely, when some not slight obstruction arises either around the kidneys and the other urinary vessels, or around certain particles that can restrain the urine so that it leaves in moderate amounts, owing to some affection; then the urine, as if strained through narrow passages, as through a filter, comes out very thin, as is seen in those who strain cloudy and thick wine and make it perfectly clear.

units.la: c. Naturæ debilitatem, atq; eò potius quò cum caloribus prauioribus spectetur.
units.tr: c. Weakness of nature, and all the more so when it is viewed together with more harmful heats.

units.la: d. Canalium urinæ læsam attractricem, qui scilicet non attrahunt nisi quod tenue est: aut si attrahunt, non nisi quod tenue est eijciunt.
units.tr: d. Impaired attractive power of the urinary passages, which, namely, attract only what is thin; or if they attract anything else, they expel only what is thin.

units.la: e. Frigiditatem uehementem cum siccitate, nempe ab utraque intemperatura tales urinas fieri est ostensum.
units.tr: e. Intense cold with dryness: it has been shown that such urines arise from both intemperaments.

units.la: In acutis morbis,
units.tr: In acute diseases,

units.la: a. Concoctricis debilitatem,
units.tr: a. Weakness of the concocting power,

units.la: b. Morbi, & succorum in venis cruditatem.
units.tr: b. Crudity of the disease and of the humours in the veins.

units.la: Si diutius perseueret,
units.tr: If it persists longer,

units.la: c. Mortem, si natura non sufficiat: abscessum in partibus inferis, si virtus valeat.
units.tr: c. Death, if nature is not sufficient; an abscess in the lower parts, if the strength prevails.

units.la: In crisi,
units.tr: In the crisis,

units.la: d. Recidiuam minatur vt in Hermocrate tertio epidemiorum.
units.tr: d. It threatens a relapse, as in Hermocrates, third book of the Epidemics.

units.la: a. b. Coctricis debilitatem, siue a nuda intemperatura fuerit, siue ob humorum excessum: nequeunte scilicet natura munia sua obire, atque ob id urina nequaquam elaborata. Inde & morbi & succorum in uenis cruditatem, nondum incumbente natura ad ipsorum concoctionem.
units.tr: a. b. Weakness of the concocting power, whether it arises from a bare intemperament or from an excess of humours: namely, since nature cannot perform its functions, and therefore the urine is not at all matured. Hence both the disease and the crudity of the humours in the veins, since nature is not yet bearing down on their concoction.

units.la: c. Mortem, si natura non sufficiat: & abscessum in partibus inferis, si uirtus ualeat. Nempe teste Galeno super prognosticum illud: Quò tenues & crudas diutius mingunt urinas. si diutius urinæ incoctæ perseuerent, definire opus, an ne æger longitudini morbi haudquaquam sufficiet, an per abscessum iudicabitur: sed definitio ex aliis fiet signis. Nempe lethalia mortem indicant, æqua autem & bona salutem.
units.tr: c. Death, if nature is not sufficient; and an abscess in the lower parts, if the strength prevails. Namely, as Galen testifies on that prognostic: "Those who pass thin and crude urines for a long time..." If undigested urines persist for a long time, the work is to determine whether the patient will by no means be equal to the length of the disease, or whether he will be judged by an abscess; but the determination will be made from other signs. Namely, deadly signs indicate death, while equal and good signs indicate health.

units.la: d. Recidiuam minatur in crisi, quòd urinæ tenues morbum esse crudum indicent.
units.tr: d. It threatens a relapse in the crisis, because thin urines indicate that the disease is still crude.

units.la: Crassa,
units.tr: Thick,

units.la: d. Pugnam naturæ cum humore,
units.tr: d. A struggle of nature with the humour,

units.la: Abundantiam humoris,
units.tr: An abundance of humour,

units.la: c. Superficiei corporis spissatione ob frigus. Si tenuis præcesserit,
units.tr: c. Thickening of the surface of the body from cold. If thin urine has come first,

units.la: d. Coctionis principium.
units.tr: d. The beginning of concoction.

units.la: Vnà cum accessu febris talis visa, neque quæ in processu crassescere desinat, aut si desierit, non tenetur,
units.tr: Together with the onset of a fever of this kind, and not one that stops thickening as it goes on; or if it has stopped, it is not held to be...

units.la: e. Virtutis infirmitatem et multitudinem humorum non paruam.
units.tr: e. Weakness of strength and a not small multitude of humours.

units.la: a. Pugnam naturæ cum humore : naturæ scilicet veluti intentæ ut materiæ dominetur, atq; iamiam forte dominantis, nisi vehementer crassæ apparuerint, hinc & abundantiam humoris.
units.tr: a. A struggle of nature with the humour: nature, namely, as if intent on mastering the matter, and perhaps about to dominate it, unless the urines appear very thick; hence also an abundance of humour.

units.la: c. Superficiei corporis spissationem ob frigus, nempe quòd ob frigus transpiratio prohibita sit, crassiores apparent urinæ.
units.tr: c. Thickening of the surface of the body from cold: namely, because from cold the transpiration is prevented, and the urines appear thicker.

units.la: d. Coctionis principium, si tenuis præcesserit. Nam si urinæ apparuerint tenues & non ob aliquâ nudam intemperaturam, nunquam ad mediocritatem mutabuntur, nisi prius ingenita fuerit crassitudo.
units.tr: d. The beginning of concoction, if thin urine has come first. For if urines have appeared thin, and not from some bare intemperament, they will never change to moderation unless the thickness has first been generated within.

units.la: e. Virtutis infirmitatem, & multitudinem humorum non paruam, cum scilicet vehementer crassæ fuerint, subacta scilicet à tanta materia natura.
units.tr: e. Weakness of strength and a not small multitude of humours, namely when the urines have been very thick, since nature has been overcome by so great a quantity of matter.

units.la: Crassa bifariam est,
units.tr: Thick is twofold,

units.la: Pellucida, Turbida.
units.tr: Clear, Turbid.

units.la: Crassa pellucida,
units.tr: Thick and clear,

units.la: Pituitæ vitreæ resolutionem, ut in epileptico rum ex pituita vrinis apparet.
units.tr: The resolution of glassy phlegm, as appears in epileptics from phlegm in the urine.

units.la: Citrina si fuerit, Cholen vitellinam.
units.tr: If it is yellow, the yolk-coloured bile.

units.la: Horum rationes maximè inquisitoribus non in expertis constant. Nam crassæ urinæ semper fuère signa humorum quorumcunque aliquo pacto in plentium uentrem, & intestina, atque hepatis cauas partes.
units.tr: The reasons for these are chiefly not established for those who investigate without experience. For thick urines have always been signs of humours of whatever kind, in some way, in the belly and intestines and in the hollow parts of the liver.

units.la: Turbida crassa,
units.tr: Turbid and thick,

units.la: Crudam cum flatuoso spiritu multo turbationem,
units.tr: Much turbidity from crude, windy spirit,

units.la: Copiam humorum qui natura expelluntur,
units.tr: A quantity of humours that nature expels,

units.la: Naturæ laborem in segregando & expellendo.
units.tr: Labour of nature in separating and expelling.

units.la: Sed tribus consideratur modis:
units.tr: But it is considered in three ways:

units.la: nam vel
units.tr: for either

units.la: Turbida micta paulò post residet,
units.tr: The turbid urine settles a little after being passed,

units.la: vel
units.tr: or

units.la: Semper similis manet,
units.tr: It remains always similar,

units.la: vel
units.tr: or

units.la: Pura mingitur, & postea conturbatur.
units.tr: It is passed clear, and afterwards becomes cloudy.

units.la: Prima,
units.tr: The first,

units.la: Parum aliquid turbulentiæ inæqualis superesse ostendit.
units.tr: Shows that some slight unequal turbulence remains.

units.la: Secunda,
units.tr: The second,

units.la: Vigere adhuc eam quæ in sanguine est agitationem, & crudorum humorum craf- fitiem vltra fluctuosam turbationem.
units.tr: Shows that the agitation still prevailing in the blood, and the thickness of the crude humours, are still at work beyond the fluctuating turbidity.

units.la: Tertia,
units.tr: The third,

units.la: Iam crudi succi coctionem aggredi naturam.
units.tr: Shows that nature has now begun the concoction of the crude juice.

units.la: Turbidarum omnium generalis nota.
units.tr: The general mark of all turbid urines.

units.la: Crassi a liquidiore separatio, aut propere, aut tarde facta, aut prorsus nulla.
units.tr: Separation of the thick from the thinner part, made either quickly, or slowly, or not at all.

units.la: *Nulla dictum est: nam uehementer crassa a materiae copia subactam naturam succubuisse, ut ante dictum est. Haec de turbidis urinis dicta sunt ex Galeni quarto de sanitate tuenda.
units.tr: Nulla: it has been said that, for urines very thick from an abundance of matter, nature has yielded, having been overcome, as was said before. These things about turbid urines have been said from Galen's fourth book on preserving health.

units.la: Vrina mediocris non pellucida vt aqua, neque turbida, vt subiugalium,
units.tr: Moderate urine, neither clear like water nor turbid like that of draught animals,

units.la: Sanitatem.
units.tr: indicates health.

units.la: IVDICIVM EX VRINA- rum quantitate.
units.tr: JUDGMENT FROM THE QUANTITY OF THE URINE.

units.la: Multa in sanis,
units.tr: Many things in healthy people:

units.la: a. Vini aquei exuberantem potionem,
units.tr: a. A copious drinking of watery wine,

units.la: b. Ciborum humidiorum vsum,
units.tr: b. Use of moister foods,

units.la: Ventris excretionem paucam,
units.tr: A small evacuation by the bowels,

units.la: d. Diureticorum vsum nimium,
units.tr: d. Excessive use of diuretics,

units.la: e. Ciborum crudorum concoctionem.
units.tr: e. Digestion of raw foods.

units.la: a.b. Vini aquei exuberantem potionem, & cibo-rum humidiorum usum, quod cibi boni & humi-diores maximè omnium & nutriunt & defluunt: unum uero potius quàm cætera nutrit, atque citi-us disperditur.
units.tr: a.b. Copious drinking of watery wine and use of moister foods, because good and moister foods most of all both nourish and flow away: the one nourishes more than the others, and is dispersed more quickly.

units.la: d. Diureticorum nimium usum, quod sua calidi-tate moueant urinæ multitudinem, subtilitate ue-rò cruditatem humorum diuidant, atque pharma-corum proprietate efficiant, ut per urinam potius seducantur.
units.tr: d. Excessive use of diuretics, because by their heat they stir up a quantity of urine, and by their thinness they divide the crudity of the humours, and by the property of the drugs they bring it about that the humours are drawn off through the urine rather.

units.la: e. Ciborum crudorum concoctionem, quòd concoctæ materiæ superfluitates humidæ seduce-cantur.
units.tr: e. Digestion of raw foods, because the moist superfluities of the digested matter are drawn off.

units.la: In ægris multa,
units.tr: In the sick, many things:

units.la: a. Diabetem, id est, vrinæ transsitum, b. Superfluitatum excretionem, c. Corporis colliquationem, d, Terminationem ægritudinis, e. Ventris siccitatem.
units.tr: a. Diabetes, that is, the passing of urine, b. Excretion of superfluities, c. Wasting of the body, d. Termination of the illness, e. Dryness of the bowels.

units.la: a. Diabetem quidem, intemperatura scilicet exauctæ caliditatis circa renes id efficiente.
units.tr: a. Diabetes indeed, the intemperature of an excessive heat about the kidneys, namely, bringing this about.

units.la: b. c. d. Superfluitatum excretionem, & termina-tionem ægritudinis, atq; corporis colliquationè: dissolutis scilicet humoribus & ad urinas exitum festinantibus.
units.tr: b. c. d. Excretion of superfluities, and termination of the illness, and wasting of the body: namely, when the humours are dissolved and hasten to exit by the urine.

units.la: e. Ventris siccitatem, humoribus alio transflu-entibus.
units.tr: e. Dryness of the bowels, when the humours flow over to another place.

units.la: In acutis febribus multa,
units.tr: In acute fevers, many things:

units.la: a. Febris solutionem,
units.tr: a. Resolution of the fever,

units.la: b. Conuersionem in hecticam,
units.tr: b. Conversion into hectic fever,

units.la: c. Conuulsionem.
units.tr: c. Convulsion.

units.la: a. Febris solutionem, nempe ut nō raro per uen trem uniuersum corpus repurgatur: & item quoq; per renes & uesicam, ut ex statu secundo primi li- bri de morbis uulgaribus.
units.tr: a. Resolution of the fever, namely, that not seldom the whole body is purged through sweat; and likewise through the kidneys and bladder, as in the second status of the first book of Of Common Diseases.

units.la: b. Conuersionem in hecticam, dissolutis scilicet corporis humiditatibus & per urinas delatis, si nō subsecuta fuerit alleuatio.
units.tr: b. Conversion into hectic fever, namely, when the moistures of the body are dissolved and carried off through the urine, if no relief follows.

units.la: c. Conuulsionem, ex inflammatione scilicet ab ea dissolutis humiditatibus.
units.tr: c. Convulsion, namely from inflammation, with the moistures dissolved by it.

units.la: Vrina pauca,
units.tr: Scanty urine,

units.la: a. Diætam ficciorem,
units.tr: a. A drier diet,

units.la: b. Ciborum tenacium & crassiorum vsum,
units.tr: b. Use of tenacious and thicker foods,

units.la: c. Obstructiones,
units.tr: c. Obstructions,

units.la: d. Ventris cuacuationem multam,
units.tr: d. Great evacuation by the bowels,

units.la: e. Febris vehementiam,
units.tr: e. Vehemence of fever,

units.la: f. Laesionem vasorum vrinalium.
units.tr: f. Injury to the urinary vessels.

units.la: a. Diætam ficciorem, id est, cibos ficciores, pauci tatem potus, exercitium uehemens, & cætera quæ desiccare consueuerunt.
units.tr: a. A drier diet, that is, drier foods, scantiness of drink, vehement exercise, and other things which are accustomed to dry up.

units.la: b. c. Ciborum tenacium & crasiorum usum, quod meatus claudant, & exinde obstructione pa riant.
units.tr: b. c. Use of tenacious and thicker foods, because they close the passages and thereby give rise to obstruction.

units.la: d. Ventris euacuationem multam: nam cum natura totam superfluitatem per consuetos meatus uacuare soleat, si forte alter alterum uacuatione superauerit, per alterū minor quatitas uacuabitur.
units.tr: d. A great evacuation by the bowels: for since nature is accustomed to empty the whole superfluity through the usual passages, if perhaps one evacuation outdoes the other, a smaller quantity will be emptied through the other.

units.la: e. Febris uehementiam, atq; ob id tostum humo rem, (ex epidemijs) cōsumpta scilicet à calore corporis humiditate.
units.tr: e. Vehemence of fever, and therefore the humour is consumed (from the epidemics), namely the moisture being used up by the heat of the body.

units.la: f. Læsionem uasorum urinalium, ob scilicet imbecillitatem uirtutis excretiuæ, uel renum uel aliorum urinæ instrumentorum.
units.tr: f. Injury to the urinary vessels, namely from weakness of the excretory power, either of the kidneys or of the other urinary organs.

units.la: IVDICIA EX VRINARUM coloribus.
units.tr: JUDGEMENTS FROM THE COLOURS OF URINE.

units.la: Alba, crystallea, & aquosa.
units.tr: White, crystalline and watery.

units.la: a. Cruditatem à frigiditate, b. Coctricis facultatis imbecillitatem, c. Meatuum urinæ fortem opilationem, d. Tingentis humoris auersionem, e. Potus magnitudinem.
units.tr: a. Crudity from cold; b. weakness of the concocting faculty; c. strong obstruction of the urinary passages; d. aversion of the tinging humour; e. quantity of drink.

units.la: a. Cruditatem à frigiditate, uel ingenita uel mor bosa.
units.tr: a. Crudity from cold, whether innate or morbid.

units.la: b. Coctricis facultatis imbecillitatem, natura scilicet ob imbecillitatem sese erigere ad coctionem nequeunte.
units.tr: b. Weakness of the concocting faculty: nature, too weak to raise itself to concoction, cannot do it.

units.la: c. Meatuum urinæ fortem oppilationem, nonnunquam & hepatis: sed à loci dolore discernitur.
units.tr: c. Strong obstruction of the urinary passages, sometimes also of the liver; but it is distinguished by pain in the place.

units.la: d. Tingentis humoris auersionem, ut in febre ardente quæ ob bilis copiam fit: cuius colore si urina non tingitur, constat bilem in uasis non permanere, sed ad cerebrū ob leuitatē ascendere. Quòd si in his phrenitis non adsit, scito iam proxime futuram. Id etiam patet in dysenterijs & alijs abscessibus.
units.tr: d. Aversion of the tinging humour, as in burning fever, which arises from an abundance of bile. If the urine is not tinged by that colour, it is clear that the bile does not remain in the vessels but rises to the brain because of its lightness. If phrenitis is not present in these cases, know that it will soon come. This is also evident in dysenteries and other abscesses.

units.la: e. Potus magnitudinem, in sanis maximè, & præsertim uini exilis. Glauca & charopa,a. Virtutis concoctricis debilitatem.
units.tr: e. Quantity of drink, especially in healthy people, and particularly of thin wine. Glaucous and charopa [χαροπά]: a. weakness of the concocting power.

units.la: In febrium initijs & incrementis,b. Labores:
units.tr: In the beginnings and increases of fevers: b. labours.

units.la: In febrium declinatione,c. Salutem.
units.tr: In the decline of fevers: c. health.

units.la: Alba muccosa,Phlegmatis humorisque crudi abundantiam.
units.tr: White and mucous: abundance of phlegm and crude humour.

units.la: Alba pinguis,Pinguitudinis colliquationem.
units.tr: White and fatty: melting of fat.

units.la: Alba lactì acetoso similis,Phlegmatis liquefactionem, præsentem vel futuram.
units.tr: White, like sour milk: liquefaction of phlegm, present or future.

units.la: In acutis,Mortem aut phthisim.
units.tr: In acute illnesses: death or phthisis.

units.la: Alba vt fungus, si cum sanie,Vlcus in vrinæ instrumentis.
units.tr: White, like a fungus, if with pus: an ulcer in the urinary organs.

units.la: Si absque sanie,Materiæ crudæ multæ separationem,Lapidem item vesicæ.
units.tr: If without pus: separation of much crude matter; also a stone in the bladder.

units.la: Genituræ similis. i. alba & crassa,Phlegmatis vitrei vacuationem. Hippocrates sexto epidemiorum de ea agit.
units.tr: Like semen, that is, white and thick: evacuation of vitreous phlegm. Hippocrates treats of this in the sixth book of the Epidemics.

units.la: Alba in ictero perseuerante, Hydropem.
units.tr: White in persistent jaundice: dropsy.

units.la: a. Virtutis concoctricis debilitatem, natura humores alterare & coquere nequeunte.
units.tr: a. Weakness of the concocting faculty, since nature cannot alter and concoct the humours.

units.la: b. Labores, ob scilicet multitudinis materiæ putrefactæ augmentum.
units.tr: b. Labours, namely because of the increase of putrefied matter.

units.la: c. Salutem, nempe febris declinationem, præsertim cum præcedentes urinæ fuerint magis aureæ. Cætera ex Auicenna sunt petenda.
units.tr: c. Health, namely a decline of the fever, especially when the earlier urines were more golden. The rest is to be sought from Avicenna.

units.la: Subspicea & spicea,
units.tr: Somewhat straw-coloured and straw-coloured,

units.la: d. Minorem incoctionem quàm albæ,
units.tr: d. Less concoction than white,

units.la: b. Febris solutionem.
units.tr: b. Solution of the fever.

units.la: a. Minorem incoctionem quàm albæ, quasi natu ra coctioni indulgeat.
units.tr: a. Less concoction than white, as if nature yielded to concoction.

units.la: b. Febris solutionem, si ardentiores præcesserint febres: nempe corporis habitus ad frigidiorē concedit qualitatem.
units.tr: b. Solution of the fever, if hotter fevers have gone before: namely, the habit of the body yields to a cooler quality.

units.la: Subaurea & subcrocea, vel sufflava, & subruffa, In iuuenibus,
units.tr: Somewhat golden and somewhat saffron, or yellowish, and somewhat reddish, in young people,

units.la: a. Perfectam concoctionem, & corporis totius certam sanitatem.
units.tr: a. Perfect concoction and certain health of the whole body.

units.la: In senibus & mulieribus,
units.tr: In old people and women,

units.la: b. Habitudinem ad qualitatem acutiorem versam.
units.tr: b. A habit turned towards a sharper quality.

units.la: a. Perfectam concoctionem, nempe ubi medioꝑris concoction fit, crocea tum atque aurea bilis generatur: & urinæ apparent subcroceæ atque subaureæ, colore bilis remisso ob mixtionem sereæ humiditatis, cuius color est albus.
units.tr: a. Perfect concoction, namely where medium concoction takes place, and then saffron and golden bile is generated; and the urines appear somewhat saffron and somewhat golden, the colour of the bile being subdued by the mixture of serous moisture, whose colour is white.

units.la: b. Habitudinem ad qualitatem acutiorem uersam, nempe senibus & mulieribus, ob ingenitam quandam frigidam temperaturam, urinæ sunt sub spiceæ. Versionem hanc fieri constat propter assiduas rerum acutarum esus, aut exercitationes immodicas.
units.tr: b. A habit turned towards a sharper quality, namely in old people and women, who have an innate cold temperament; their urines are straw-coloured. It is established that this change comes from constant use of sharp foods or from immoderate exercise.

units.la: Aurea & crocea,
units.tr: Golden and saffron,

units.la: a. Caliditatis intensionem quandam. Aurea, b. Potius per materiæ quantitate, quam per materiæ defectum. Crocea, c. Contrario modo.
units.tr: a. An intensification of heat of some kind. Golden; b. more from the quantity of matter than from its deficiency. Saffron; c. in the opposite way.

units.la: a. Caliditatis intensionem quandam, in iuuenibus ob minores occasiones: in senibus & mulieribus ob maiores.
units.tr: a. An intensification of heat of some kind: in young people from slighter causes, in old people and women from greater ones.

units.la: b. Per materiæ quantitatem, nempe aurea apparet ob multorum ciborum & medicinarum acutarum oblationem: item ob sanguinis ebullitionem ab ira, item ob intemperaturā quandam calidā uisceris, item ob affectu quendam anni similem.
units.tr: b. From the quantity of matter: namely, golden colour appears from taking many foods and sharp medicines; likewise from the boiling up of blood through anger; likewise from a certain hot intemperance of an organ; likewise from a certain affection like that of the season of the year.

units.la: c. Contrario modo dictum est, nempe crocea apparet ob mœrorem, curam, uigilias, ob Solis æstu, ob laborem, & similia.
units.tr: c. It has been said in the opposite way: saffron appears from sorrow, care, wakefulness, the heat of the sun, labour, and similar things.

units.la: Russa, a. Flauæ bilis abundantiam, vel ipsius syncē-ritatem.
units.tr: Russet, a. Abundance of yellow bile, or its very purity.

units.la: Russa & tenuis,
units.tr: Russet and thin,

units.la: b. Morbum crudum.
units.tr: b. Crude disease.

units.la: a. Bilem & russam & pallidam & flauam nominant, nam bilis albior & turbulentior facta ruffescit: si uero splendens sit & purior, flauescit. Ergo russus color ad album magis, flauus ad splendidū magis uergit. Pallidus color russo albior, unde Galenus in primo de iudicationibus: quātō flauo ruf-sum est albius, tantò illo pallidum. hic accipimus pallidum croceum ut Ochra est.
units.tr: a. They call bile both russet and pale and yellow. For bile, when it becomes whiter and more turbid, turns reddish; but if it is shining and purer, it turns yellow. So russet colour tends more towards white, yellow more towards bright. Pale colour is whiter than russet, whence Galen in the first book of On Crises says: by as much as russet is whiter than yellow, by so much is the pale whiter than that. Here we take pale to mean saffron, as ochre is.

units.la: b. Morbum crudū, & maximè quatenus tenuis substantiæ.
units.tr: b. Crude disease, especially as far as it is of thin substance.

units.la: Subrubens,
units.tr: Somewhat red,

units.la: a. Sanguinis non exquisitè cocti abundantiam,
units.tr: a. Abundance of blood not thoroughly concocted,

units.la: b. Bilis rubræ mixtionem.
units.tr: b. Mixture of red bile.

units.la: a. Sanguinis non exquisitè cocti abundantiam, ubi enim sanguinis serum una cum urina emittitur, uidetur & colore subrubens, cum igitur tum humidior tum serosior sit, coctione eget.
units.tr: a. Abundance of blood not thoroughly concocted: when the serum of the blood is emitted together with the urine, the urine also appears somewhat red in colour. Since it is then both moister and more serous, it needs concoction.

units.la: b. Bilis rubræ mixtionem nouerunt, qui subrubras uidēre & deiectiones & urinas.
units.tr: b. Those who see somewhat red stools and urines know the mixture of red bile.

units.la: Rubens,
units.tr: Red,

units.la: a. Bilis rubræ multitudinem,
units.tr: a. Great quantity of red bile,

units.la: b. Sanguinis saniem multam,
units.tr: b. Much pus of the blood,

units.la: c. Sanguinis crudioris et serosioris abundantiam. Crassa eadem & nihil deponens,
units.tr: c. Abundance of cruder and more serous blood. The same, thick and depositing nothing,

units.la: d. Turbationem crudam multo praedita spiri tu flatuoso.
units.tr: d. Crude turbidity accompanied by much flatulent breath.

units.la: Crassa eadem, inde tenuis, ante cri-sim & post crisim,
units.tr: The same, thick, then thin, before crisis and after crisis,

units.la: e. Recidiuam.
units.tr: e. Relapse.

units.la: Rubens in iclero ita ut pannum tingat,
units.tr: Red in jaundice, so that it stains cloth,

units.la: f. Salutem.
units.tr: f. Health.

units.la: Rubens modice,
units.tr: Moderately red,

units.la: g. Hydropem futurum.
units.tr: g. Future dropsy.

units.la: a. Bilis rubrae multitudo maxime patet in iuue-nibus.
units.tr: a. A great quantity of red bile is seen especially in young people.

units.la: b. Sanguinis sanies multa etiam constat, nempe abundante sanguine si non flabelletur, sanies quae dam generatur, qualis est uligo illa quae in corpori bus humidioribus quotidie spectatur ubi putre-scunt, sanies igitur illa cum urinis expellitur.
units.tr: b. Much pus of the blood is also evident. Namely, when the blood is abundant and is not cooled by fanning, some pus is generated, such as the damp that is seen every day in moister bodies where they rot; that pus is therefore expelled with the urine.

units.la: c. Sanguinis crudioris & serosioris abundantia in ardentibus reperitur febribus, ubi diuturnior est morbus, tempore indigens ad maturationem. Vbi itaque amplior semicrudus sanguis per urinam ex pellitur, rubram eum hanc efficere ratio couincit: ut patet in Hermocrate tertij epidemiorum.
units.tr: c. Abundance of cruder and more serous blood is found in burning fevers, where the disease is more prolonged and needs time for maturation. Where therefore a larger amount of half-cooked blood is expelled through the urine, reason shows that this makes it red, as is evident in Hermocrates in the third book of the Epidemics.

units.la: d. Turbationem crudam multo praeditam spiri-tu flatuoso, ut in musto fieri solet. Hae autem uri-nae conturbatae & turbidę dicuntur, quibus capitis dolores sunt adiuncti, spiritu flatuoso cum calidioribus succis petente: eadem in Hermocrate uisa est.
units.tr: d. Crude turbidity furnished with much flatulent spirit, as usually happens in new wine. These urines are called disturbed and turbid, and they are accompanied by headaches, since the flatulent spirit seeks out hotter juices. The same was seen in Hermocrates.

units.la: e. Recidiuam, haec notissima est ex eodem Hermocrate.
units.tr: e. Relapse: this is best known from the same Hermocrates.

units.la: f.g. Salutem in his expectare oportet, nondum scilicet imbecillitato hepate hydropem futurum: nempe tunc cum modice rubeat aut albae sint, hoc accidit ex hepatis debilitate.
units.tr: f.g. In these cases one must expect health; dropsy is not yet to come, since the liver is not yet weakened. Namely, when the urine is moderately red or white, this happens from weakness of the liver.

units.la: Prærubens vel rubens cruenta,
units.tr: Reddish or red, bloody,

units.la: a. Renum debilitatem, b. Sanguinis ex parte aliqua profluxum, c. Renum laxitatem immodicam, d. Sanguinis abundantiam.
units.tr: a. A weakness of the kidneys, b. a flow of blood from some part, c. an excessive looseness of the kidneys, d. an abundance of blood.

units.la: Crassa eadem & multa,
units.tr: Thick and the same, and copious,

units.la: e. Crisim & sanitatem.
units.tr: e. A crisis and health.

units.la: a. Renum debilitatem, id quod fit renibus perpetram fungentibus suo munere, sicut fieri solet in doloribus nephriticis.
units.tr: a. A weakness of the kidneys, which happens when the kidneys do not perform their function properly, as is usually the case in kidney pains.

units.la: b. Sanguinis ex parte aliqua profluxum, nempe uena incisa aliqua uel rupta circa urinae uasa talis apparet, sed loci dolore & causa antecedente dignoscitur.
units.tr: b. A flow of blood from some part: when a vein has been cut or broken somewhere around the urinary vessels, the urine appears bloody in this way, but it is recognised by the pain in the place and by the preceding cause.

units.la: c. Renum laxitatem immodicam, cum scilicet ua saurinam colantia raritatem habuerint, uel natura uel ob aliam causam, siquidem plerunq; cum urina secernitur sanguis.
units.tr: c. An excessive looseness of the kidneys, namely when the vessels that strain the urine have become porous, whether by nature or from some other cause, since blood is usually secreted together with the urine.

units.la: d. Sanguinis abundantiam, ut uidere est in his continuis quas synochos uocant. e. Crisim & sanitatem, nonnunquā indicare con-stat in acutis febribus & complicatis, natura scili-cet ad urinas quod molestum erat mittente.
units.tr: d. An abundance of blood, as can be seen in those continuous fevers which they call synochus. e. It is established that a crisis and health are sometimes indicated in acute and complicated fevers, when nature sends out through the urine what had been troubling the body.

units.la: Vrina �ũinea in sanis,
units.tr: Urine bloody in healthy people,

units.la: a. Sanguinis assatiónem.
units.tr: a. A boiling of the blood.

units.la: In vehementibus febribus,
units.tr: In violent fevers,

units.la: b. Sanguinis saniosi & putrescentis abun-dantiam,
units.tr: b. An abundance of foul and putrefying blood,

units.la: c. Sanguinis in rubram bilem transformatio-nem.
units.tr: c. A transformation of the blood into red bile.

units.la: a. Talis sanguinis assatio contingit sanis ob lon-gas uias ęstusq;,&ob laborec:& maximé in his qui molli sunt corpore & facilè patibili. Tales etiam urinas sæpissimè uidi in his, qui liberaliter & assi-duè bibunt uina crassa.
units.tr: a. Such a boiling of the blood happens to healthy people from long journeys, heat and labour, and especially in those who are soft of body and easily worn out. I have also very often seen such urine in those who drink thick wines freely and constantly.

units.la: b. c. Reliqua duo nota sunt propter caloris ue-hementiam.
units.tr: b. and c. The other two are well known, on account of the vehemence of the heat.

units.la: Vrina passea,
units.tr: Urine like a sparrow's or pale yellow,

units.la: Bilei humoris adustionem.
units.tr: A burning of the bilious humour.

units.la: Nempe crocea bilis exassata, atque uiolaçea esse-ęta, adeo ut ferè accipiat imaginem humoris me-lancholici, talem efficit urinam.
units.tr: Namely, when yellow bile has been burnt up and has become violet-coloured, so that it almost takes on the appearance of the melancholic humour, it produces such urine.

units.la: Vrina viridis bifariam,
units.tr: Urine green in two ways,

units.la: Viridis nomine generis,
units.tr: Green in the name of the genus,

units.la: Viridis oleacea.
units.tr: Green like oil.

units.la: Viridis ad nigredinem magis decli-nans, a. Bilis tum violaceæ tum cœruleæ multitudinem, b. Frigiditatem. Æruginosa, c. Flauæ bilis adustionem, atque in viridem conuersionem. Si perseueret cum suis malis accidentibus, d. A siccitate conuulsionem.
units.tr: Green, inclining more to blackness: a. a great quantity of bile, both violet and blue; b. coldness. Verdigris-coloured: c. a burning of yellow bile and its conversion into green. If it persists with its bad accompanying symptoms: d. convulsion from dryness.

units.la: a. Bilis tum uiolaceæ tum cœruleæ multitudine, nempe talis uiridis color bilis tum quantitatem, tum qualitatem, tum in aliud genus conuersione caliditatis excessu ostendit.
units.tr: a. A great quantity of bile, both violet and blue: such a green colour shows that the bile is abundant, both in quantity and in quality, and that it has been changed into another kind by an excess of heat.

units.la: b. Frigiditatem etiam, nempe cum niger color talis tum frigiditate tum a uehementi caliditate fiat, uiridisq; sit ad nigrum uia, ratio uincit frigiditate a uiridi significari colore.
units.tr: b. Coldness also: since a black colour of this kind arises both from coldness and from a violent heat, and since green tends towards black, reason concludes that the green colour signifies coldness.

units.la: c. Adustionem flauæ bilis, atque in uiridem conuersionem, ex æruginosa significari intelligetur qui bilem flauam, si uehementer aduratur, in nigram mutari.
units.tr: c. A burning of yellow bile and its conversion into green; from the verdigris colour it will be understood that yellow bile, if it is burnt vehemently, changes into black.

units.la: d. A siccitate conuulsionem, nempe si æruginosa bilis perseueret cum suis malis accidetibus, quæ sunt sitis asidua, æstus, lingua adusta, hypochondria retracta, uomitus, & similia: nam uirtus imbecilla si fuerit, & non remittantur colores, sequi solet conuulsio a siccitate & æstu. Id phreneticis fieri solet.
units.tr: d. Convulsion from dryness: namely, if the verdigris-coloured bile persists with its bad accompanying symptoms, which are constant thirst, fever heat, a burnt tongue, a drawn-in abdomen, vomiting and the like. For if the strength is feeble and the colours do not abate, convulsion usually follows from dryness and fever heat. This usually happens in phrenitic patients.

units.la: Oleosa ad candidius viĉo pallido verges. Humorum cruditatem.
units.tr: Oily, tending to a whiter, pale colour. A crudeness of the humours.

units.la: Vehementer pallida ut ad flauum accedat,
units.tr: Very pale, so that it approaches yellow,

units.la: Biliosum calorem.
units.tr: A bilious heat.

units.la: Cum reliquis signis salubribus,
units.tr: With the other signs favourable,

units.la: Breui tempore salutem.
units.tr: Health in a short time.

units.la: Cum malis,
units.tr: With the bad signs,

units.la: Morbi longitudinem,
units.tr: The length of the illness,

units.la: Mortem.
units.tr: Death.

units.la: Sicut (inquit Galenus in cōmentario tertij uulgarium in primi ægri, post tempestatem, enarratio ne) oleum ipsum unius neque coloris neq; crassitiei, nec item oleosa urina semel est pallida, sed plus minus: periculumq; his urinis non ob prauitatem subest, sed ob uim febris. Hinc quidam, si re liqua consentiant salubria, breui liberantur: alij morbum trahunt, alij moriuntur, ut patet de primo ægro tertij epidemiorum post tempestatem, qui sexto die oleosam habuit urinam, & centesimo uigesimo obijt.
units.tr: As (says Galen in his commentary on the third book of the Epidemics, in the exposition of the first patient after the preface) oil itself is neither of one colour nor of one thickness, so an oily urine is not always equally pale but more or less so; and the danger in such urines does not lie in their badness but in the force of the fever. Hence some, if the other things agree and are favourable, are freed quickly; others draw out the illness, and others die. This is clear from the first patient of the third book of the Epidemics, after the preface, who on the sixth day had oily urine and died on the hundred and twentieth day.

units.la: Oleosa omnis,
units.tr: Every oily urine,

units.la: Pinguis colliquationem,
units.tr: Fat, a melting away,

units.la: Caliditatem adulterinam, hecticam.
units.tr: An adulterine, hectic heat.

units.la: Cum pinguedo (inquit Aëtius) paulatim liquescat, colliquatio principium habet, incrementum, & uigorem. In principio urinæ aquosæ ne sint an oleaginæ, ambigunt, & tales ab Actuario oleicolores uocantur: in augmento insignior olei mixtura apparet, & talis oleapparens dicitur ab eodem autore: in uigore uero urinæ totæ & colore & liquore oleosæ planè sunt.
units.tr: Since fat (says Aëtius) melts away little by little, the melting away has a beginning, an increase and a vigour. At the beginning people doubt whether the urine is watery or oily, and such urines are called oil-coloured by Actuarius; in the increase a more marked mixture of oil appears, and such urine is called visibly oily by the same author; but in the vigour the whole urine is plainly oily both in colour and in liquid.

units.la: Oleosa si tradè procedit & paulatim increscat,
units.tr: If the oiliness proceeds gradually and increases little by little,

units.la: Pinguitudinis uniuersi corporis colliquationem.
units.tr: It is a melting away of the fat of the whole body.

units.la: Si breui & confertim,
units.tr: If briefly and all at once,

units.la: Solorum renum.
units.tr: Of the kidneys alone.

units.la: Nam si febris & calor ille adulterinus per totum corpus diffusus fuerit, paulatim excernitur: si calor plurimus circa renes fuerit, copiose & cumulatim fluit: ex Aëtio. Discrimē igitur inde est, quòd in priori totum corpus ardere sentitur: in posterio re soli renes.
units.tr: For if the fever and that adulterine heat is spread through the whole body, it is discharged little by little; if the greatest heat is around the kidneys, it flows abundantly and in a heap: from Aëtius. The difference, therefore, is that in the former the whole body is felt to burn, but in the latter the kidneys alone.

units.la: Oleosa post nigram,
units.tr: Oily after black,

units.la: Salutem.
units.tr: Health.

units.la: Nempe fit uersio ad melius.
units.tr: Namely, a change for the better takes place.

units.la: Oleosa in valde acutis quarto die apparens,
units.tr: Oily, appearing on the fourth day in very acute illnesses,

units.la: Septimo moriturum hominem.
units.tr: The man will die on the seventh day.

units.la: Oleosa si quid loturæ carnis simile miscetur,
units.tr: Oily, if something like the water in which meat has been washed is mixed in,

units.la: Hydropem,
units.tr: Dropsy,

units.la: Phthisim,
units.tr: Phthisis,

units.la: Colicum dolorem malum. a.b. c.Hæc ex Auicenna,si tamen quod primo loco dicitur uerum sit,inquirent qui uolent. Quod de hydrope,phthisi,&colico dolore malo dicitur, probabile est,ubi febris uehementiam sequitur he patis imbecillitas.
units.tr: A bad colic pain. a. b. c. These are from Avicenna; whether what is said in the first place is true, let those who wish to know inquire. What is said of dropsy, phthisis and bad colic pain is probable, where the severity of the fever is followed by weakness of the liver.

units.la: Veneta subtenuis, a.Fusionem humoris melancholici.
units.tr: Thin, venous: a. A melting of the melancholic humour.

units.la: Ad crassitudinem vergens, b.Frigiditatem.
units.tr: Tending to thickness: b. Coldness.

units.la: Quæ à prauis coloribus ad peiores transmutatur, c.Mortificationem.
units.tr: Which changes from bad colours to worse: c. Mortification.

units.la: Vrina liuida præter dicta de vene-ta, d.Plagas quoque & verbera homini incus-sa.
units.tr: Livid urine, besides what has been said of the venous: d. Blows and beatings inflicted on a man.

units.la: a.Fusionem humoris melancholici. nam sæpius contingit ut urinæ plus minusue tingantur, & plerunque mediocrem duntaxat suscipiant tinctură.
units.tr: a. A melting of the melancholic humour: for it often happens that urines are more or less tinged, and usually they take up only a moderate tincture.

units.la: b. Frigiditatem, nempe frigiditas non minus, quàm immodica calditas, nigrificare humores solet.
units.tr: b. Coldness: namely, coldness no less than an excessive heat tends to blacken the humours.

units.la: c.Mortificationem, maximè à frigiditate profectam:nam color niger proprius est mortuis corporibus : uenetus uerò & liuidus parum à nigro discedunt.
units.tr: c. Mortification, arising chiefly from coldness: for black is the proper colour of dead bodies, while venous and livid colours differ little from black.

units.la: d.Plagas quoq; & uerbera homini incussa,nempe liuida quę ob plagas fit,magnam indicat sanguinis factam esse mortificationem:plagis scilicet morficantibus tificantibus cadauerantibusq;, sanguis uero mortificatus subnigrescere consueuit: qui tandem a uirtute excretrice per uasa urinaria pulsus, tales procreat urinas. Caue tamen ne aliquando fallat te mulier, ut me aliquando fefellit: quæ urinæ concusi & uerberibus affecti hominis sel taurinum miscebat.
units.tr: d. Blows and beatings inflicted on a man: namely, the livid colour that comes from blows indicates that a great mortification of the blood has taken place, since the blows cause mortification, putrefaction and deadness, and the blood that has been mortified usually turns dark; this, at length driven out by the excretory power through the urinary vessels, produces such urines. Beware, however, lest a woman ever deceive you, as one once deceived me: she mixed bull's gall into the urine of a man who had been shaken and beaten.

units.la: Vrina nigra omnis continuo & crassa est, nunciatque,
units.tr: Black urine is always thick and signifies:

units.la: a. Vehemens frigus,
units.tr: a. A severe chill;

units.la: b. Mortificationem extremam,
units.tr: b. Extreme mortification;

units.la: c. Exuberantem caliditatem,
units.tr: c. Excessive heat;

units.la: d. Biliosum adustum humorem,
units.tr: d. Burnt, bilious humour;

units.la: e. Nigri excretionem humoris, & salutem.
units.tr: e. The excretion of black humour, and recovery.

units.la: a. b. Vehemens frigus, præsertim si ueneta & liui da præcesserint, frigiditatem significantes. Quod uero color is ad extremum peruenerit, ob id subiectum solet dissoluere, & ob id mortificationem extremam indicare.
units.tr: a. b. A severe chill, especially if it has been preceded by veined and livid urine, signifying coldness. But when the colour has reached the extreme, it usually dissolves the substance, and for that reason indicates extreme mortification.

units.la: c. Exuberantem, & ob id biliosum adustum consequio humorem: tales siquidem in febribus quæ causi appellantur, & phrenitidibus meiùtur, quòd tum calidæ tum siccæ affectiones eiusmodi existunt, ut constat ex prorrhetico.
units.tr: c. Excessive heat, and for that reason burnt bilious humour: for such urine is passed in fevers called causi and in phrenitis, since such affections are hot and dry, as is clear from the Prorrhetic.

units.la: d. Quòd si talis post flauam excernatur, constat a nimio calore torrefactam esse flauam bilem. Similiter accidit, si præcesserit æruginosa.
units.tr: d. But if such urine is voided after yellow urine, it is clear that the yellow bile has been scorched by excessive heat. It happens similarly if verdigris-coloured urine has gone before.

units.la: e. Nigri excretionem humoris, & salutem, tales siquidem sæpissime excernuntur in quartanarum declinatione, & melancholicis delirijs quando sol uuntur. Tales itidem lienosis plurimum excernun tur, & plerunque si pharmacum purgatiuum congruens datum sit.
units.tr: e. The excretion of black humour and recovery: such urine is very often voided at the decline of quartan fevers and in melancholic delirium when the patient is purged, and likewise it is passed very much by those with spleen disorders, and generally if a suitable purgative medicine has been given.

units.la: DE IVDICIIS VRinarum odore.
units.tr: ON THE JUDGEMENTS FROM THE SMELL OF URINE.

units.la: Vrina odore carens, a. Temperaturam frigidam, b. Cruditatem exuberantem. Et in acutis plerunque morbis, c. Naturæ mortificationem.
units.tr: Urine lacking smell signifies: (a) a cold temperament; (b) an excessive crudity; and in acute diseases, usually, (c) the mortification of nature.

units.la: a.b. c. In sanis maximè id apparere solet, quòd urinæ odore careant, cùm scilicet frigida fuerint temperatura aut superflua cruditate habuerint. Quod si contingat in morbis acutis, naturæ mortificationem, cum scilicet urina maleolens fuerit, deinde subitò talis discesserit maleolentia sine mali remissione. Odor dulcis, a. Sanguinis non putrefacti dominium. Graveolens in sanis, b. Futuram febrim ex putredine, c. Potum medicamentum. In morbis cum prauis substantia & contentis, d. Corporis habitudinem mortificatam. Si cum bonis, c. Scabiem vel vlcus in vrinæ instrumentis, & præsertim si pus fuerit.
units.tr: (a, b, c) In healthy people this is especially apparent when the urine lacks smell, namely when the temperament has been cold or they have had excessive crudity. But if it happens in acute diseases, it signifies the mortification of nature, when the urine has been foul-smelling and then suddenly that foulness has gone away without any remission of the illness. A sweet smell signifies (a) that the blood has not putrefied and is in control. A foul smell in healthy people signifies (b) a fever to come from putrefaction, or (c) that a medicine has been drunk. In diseases where the substances and contents are bad, it signifies (d) that the habit of the body is mortified. If the contents are good, it signifies (c) scabies or an ulcer in the urinary organs, especially if there is pus.

units.la: Si acris odor fuerit,
units.tr: If the smell is sharp,

units.la: f. Frigidorum humorum putrefactionem, Caloris naturalis mortem.
units.tr: it signifies (f) the putrefaction of cold humours and the death of the natural heat.

units.la: a. Sanguinis non putrefacti dominium, nempe sanguis suapte natura calidus & humidus & dulcis existit.
units.tr: (a) The blood has not putrefied and is in control: for blood is by its nature warm, moist and sweet.

units.la: b. Futuram febrim ex putredine, nempe maleolentia omnis putredinis est nota.
units.tr: (b) A fever to come from putrefaction: for every foul smell is a sign of putrefaction.

units.la: c. Potum medicamentum, nempe ut terebinthina pota urinam reddit uiolarum odoris, ita cardui radix pota crassam facit urinam & maleolentem, ut refert Aëtius in octauo.
units.tr: (c) That a medicine has been drunk: thus, as turpentine drunk makes the urine smell of violets, so the root of the thistle, drunk, makes the urine thick and foul-smelling, as Aëtius reports in book eight.

units.la: d. Corporis habitudinem mortificatam, uictus siquidem calor natiuus uictore externo.
units.tr: (d) The habit of the body is mortified, since the native heat is overcome by an external victor.

units.la: e. Scabiem uel ulcus aut quamuis aliam plagam id quod unà ostendunt causæ antecedentes & dolor topicus.
units.tr: (e) Scabies, an ulcer, or any other sore: which the preceding causes and local pain show together.

units.la: f. Frigidorum humorum putrefactionem, quòd frigidi humores si putrefiant, in acorem transeant. Id ostendit pituita, ostendit & melancholia.
units.tr: (f) The putrefaction of cold humours: for if cold humours putrefy, they turn into sourness. Phlegm shows this, and melancholy shows it too.

units.la: DE IVDICIIS EX MODO meiendi.
units.tr: ON THE JUDGEMENTS FROM THE MANNER OF URINATING.

units.la: Difficilis,
units.tr: Difficult,

units.la: a. Acrimoniam vrinæ,
units.tr: a. Sharpness of the urine;

units.la: b. Vesicæ exulcerationem, & aliquando debilitatem,
units.tr: b. Ulceration of the bladder, and sometimes weakness;

units.la: c. Phlegmonem,d. Calculum.
units.tr: c. Phlegmon; d. Stone.

units.la: Renibus aut hepate affectis,e. Abscessus ruptionem,f. Vesicæ intemperiem, vel conuulsionem.
units.tr: When the kidneys or liver are affected: e. Rupture of an abscess; f. Disorder (intemperies) of the bladder, or convulsion.

units.la: In febribus,
units.tr: In fevers,

units.la: g. Totius neruosæ partis affectum.
units.tr: g. Affection of the whole nervous part.

units.la: a. Acrimoniam urinæ, stranguriæ causam esse cõ stat Galeno in secundam tempestatem primi epide miorum, quòd scilicet uesica uellicaretur, & assi-dua excretione acris humoris solicitaretur.
units.tr: a. That sharpness of the urine is the cause of strangury Galen affirms in the second epidemic constitution of the first book of the Epidemics, namely because the bladder is irritated and constantly goaded by the excretion of a sharp humour.

units.la: b. Vesicæ exulcerationem, nempe hanc consequi tur urinæ emittendæ difficultas ex Aëtio & aliis: & aliquando debilitatem, uesica scilicet urinæ copia exprimere nequeunte.
units.tr: b. That ulceration of the bladder follows, namely difficulty in passing urine, is taken from Aëtius and others; and sometimes weakness, since the bladder, unable to expel the quantity of urine, is of course unable to do so.

units.la: c. Phlegmonem, nam qui ita afficiuntur, urinam eijcere non possunt uijs ob inflammationem com-pressis.
units.tr: c. Phlegmon: for those so affected cannot expel urine, the passages being compressed by the inflammation.

units.la: d. Calculum, eo scilicet meatus obturante.
units.tr: d. Stone: namely, when the outlet is blocked by it.

units.la: e. Abscessus ruptionem, nempe cum abscessus rumpitur, & pus per uesicam excernitur, assiduam irritationem ad mictionem propter acredinem in-ducit.
units.tr: e. Rupture of an abscess: namely, when the abscess bursts and pus is discharged through the bladder, it induces constant irritation to urinate on account of the sharpness.

units.la: f. Vesicæ intemperiem, nempe uel à frigida uel calida uesicæ propria læditur actio: conuulsio præ terea meiendi difficultatem adferre solet.
units.tr: f. Disorder of the bladder: namely, whether the proper action of the bladder is harmed by cold or by heat; convulsion, moreover, is wont to bring on difficulty in urinating.

units.la: g. Totius partis neruosæ affectû, id in febriû ma lignarum principio accidere solet, ut uesica affliga tur, & paulatim cum dolore urinam emittat, quod illi accidit affectus participatione: nam uesica ner-uosa est.
units.tr: g. Affection of the whole nervous part: this is wont to occur at the beginning of malignant fevers, so that the bladder is afflicted and gradually passes urine with pain; this happens to it by participation of the affection, for the bladder is nervous.

units.la: Meiendi modus inuoluntarius, a. Vesicam exolutam, b. Musculi vesicæ collum claudentis paralysim vel exolutionem.
units.tr: Involuntary manner of urinating: a. the bladder relaxed; b. paralysis or relaxation of the muscle closing the neck of the bladder.

units.la: a Vesicam exolutam, cum scilicet uirtus contentrix oblæsa fuerit.
units.tr: a. A relaxed bladder, namely when its retentive power has been injured.

units.la: b. Musculi uesicæ collum claudentis exolutionem, cum scilicet nerui qui ex spinali medulla ad musculum illum deferuntur, læsi fuerint.
units.tr: b. Relaxation of the muscle closing the neck of the bladder, namely when the nerves that pass from the spinal marrow to that muscle have been injured.

units.la: Miction cum dolore, Inflammationem, Abscessum, Vlcerationem, Inæqualem intemperiem, Spiritum flatuosum.
units.tr: Urination with pain: inflammation, abscess, ulceration, unequal disorder (intemperies), flatulent spirit.

units.la: Hæc notiora quàm explicari debeant.
units.tr: These are better known than they need to be explained.

units.la: DE IVDICIIS EX VRINArum contentis.
units.tr: ON THE JUDGEMENTS FROM THE CONTENTS OF URINES.

units.la: Contenta trifariam diuisa. Quæ in fundum matulæ descendunt, hypostases dicuntur, id est, subiecta. Quæ ad medium concesserunt, eneoremata, idest, sublationes vel sublimia vel suspensa. Quæ verò ad superficiem peruenerunt, nubes vel nebulæ, habentes in vrinis proportionem, quam habent in aëre nubes. Neq; hic vllum latere oportet, eınaoremata etiam nubes aliquā do ab Hippocrate dici. Sunt autem contenta supersluitates quædam tertiæ concoctionis.
units.tr: The contents are divided into three kinds. Those that sink to the bottom of the flask are called hypostases, that is, sediments. Those that rise to the middle are eneoremata, that is, lifted, or suspended, matters. Those that reach the surface are clouds or mists, having in urine the same relation that clouds have in the air. Nor should it be overlooked here that Hippocrates sometimes also calls the eneoremata clouds. The contents are, moreover, superfluities of the third concoction.

units.la: Vrina contentis priuata,
units.tr: Urine deprived of contents,

units.la: a. Dolores ingentes, Immensa exercitia, Longas vigilias, b. Materiæ defectum, c. Inflammationem calidam in principalibus membris, d. Incoctionem extremam, e. Obstructionem. f. Ventris euacuationem insignem. g. Multam materiæ corruptionem, h. Membri alicuius imbecillitatem ingenitam.
units.tr: From: a. great pains, immense exercises, long vigils; b. lack of matter; c. hot inflammation in the principal members; d. extreme under-concoction; e. obstruction; f. remarkable evacuation of the belly; g. much corruption of matter; h. innate weakness of some member.

units.la: a. Dolores ingentes, uel quòd superflua à doloribus trahantur, uel quòd uirtutem prosternat dolores, quo fit ut non munus suum coquendi expleat: sunt etenim contenta tertiæ coctionis superflua, ut dictum. Idem efficiunt uigiliæ longæ. Immensa exercitia, nam quæ per urinas excernerentur, exercitatione per sudores eliciuntur & euaporationes. rationes.
units.tr: a. Great pains, either because superfluities are drawn off by the pains, or because pain prostrates the strength, so that it cannot fulfil its office of concocting. For the contents are superfluities of the third concoction, as said. Long vigils have the same effect. Immense exercises: for what would otherwise be excreted in the urine is driven out through sweat and vapours by exercise.

units.la: b. Materiæ defectum. nam ubi egestas sit, nihil su perflui excerni potest.
units.tr: b. Lack of matter: for where there is poverty, no superfluity can be excreted.

units.la: c. Inflammatio item calida in membro aliquo principali, ob multam caliditatem superfluitates attrahit cucurbitulæ modo.
units.tr: c. Likewise hot inflammation in some principal member, which, because of its great heat, draws superfluities to itself like cupping-glasses.

units.la: d. Incoctionem extremam, propter quam absq; contentis producantur urinæ: li enim talia nō spe-ctentur, iam defecit concoctio.
units.tr: d. Extreme under-concoction, on account of which urines are produced without contents: for if such things are not seen, concoction has already failed.

units.la: e. Obstructionem, crassioribus scilicet humoribus in uia hærentibus.
units.tr: e. Obstruction, namely when thicker humours stick in the passages.

units.la: f. Ventris euacuationem insignem, humoribus superfluis alio migrantibus ad uentrem scilicet. Fit quoque id ob imbecillitatem, quæ ex euacuatio-ne uirtuti accidit concoctrici.
units.tr: f. Remarkable evacuation of the belly, when superfluous humours migrate elsewhere, namely to the belly. This also happens through weakness, which comes upon the concocting strength from the evacuation.

units.la: g. Multam materiæ corruptionem, a qua nihil commodi natura in alimentum sumere posit.
units.tr: g. Much corruption of matter, from which nature can take nothing useful as nourishment.

units.la: h. Membri alicuius imbecillitate, ob quam ad ip sum omne inutile expellitur: nempe grauatum nō solum non repellit quod influxit, uerum quoque & suscipit quod influit.
units.tr: h. Weakness of some member, on account of which everything useless is expelled to it: for the weakened member not only does not repel what has flowed in, but also receives what flows in.

units.la: In sanis, Cruditates, Obstructiones. Et si protraxerint, Futuram ægritudinem.
units.tr: In the healthy: crudities, obstructions. And if they have dragged on: a future illness.

units.la: Horum rationes in promptu sunt, & maximè huius quod tertio dictum est loco nempe diuturnis cruditatibus & oppilationibus uix resistere ho mo sanus potest.
units.tr: The reasons for these are at hand, and especially that of the third point mentioned, namely that a healthy man can hardly resist lasting crudities and obstructions.

units.la: In acutorum principijs augmentisque,
units.tr: In the beginnings and increases of acute diseases:
